Being a fan of PSU as a child, I was hyped to play the Base game [PSO2] years ago. I spent ages on this game when It hit global, finally glad they actually did it, and rubbed it in those who had no hope for a western release. Fast forward to a few years, I was surprised to hear that New Genesis was coming.

Never thought PSO2 would get a PSO'3' in a sense, so when I played the demo, I was really hyped.
When the full game released I was... questionable to say the least. the lack of content really threw people off.

I was also happy that the original game retained the data. But I will say this hot take: New Genesis has superior combat, while PSO2 has the better story. Not bashing the story of NGS, it HAS grown on me, but it took a while. NGS gives you so much better movement and the combo game is satisfying and the open world brims with enemies and wandering bosses. There are points of interest with lore and crates. Multi Weapons also spices up the combo game even more, even allowing you to use weapons as classes that can't use them, (you just can't use Photon Arts) The sad part about NGS is that you don't have as many photon arts in PSO2, removing the customization of skills. But the skills we have in NGS is pretty good. 

I do suggest if you're just getting this game. Play PSO2 FIRST, not New Genesis. The basic mechanics doesn't change between the two.

Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis (PSO2: NGS) delivers an expansive overhaul of the PSO2 formula with a focus on open-world exploration, dynamic combat, and stunning visuals. Set 1,000 years after the original, the game introduces a seamless world filled with diverse biomes, encouraging exploration through its fast-paced traversal mechanics like gliding and sprinting.

The combat system is a standout, blending action-oriented gameplay with a variety of customizable classes, keeping encounters engaging. However, players have noted that while the visuals and mechanics are impressive, the content depth at launch felt limited, with sparse endgame activities and repetitive grind for progression. Updates have gradually addressed these issues, but some long-term fans still miss the denser content of the original PSO2.

Overall, PSO2: NGS is a visually stunning and enjoyable experience for newcomers, though returning fans might find it a mixed bag depending on their expectations for depth and content variety. It’s a game worth revisiting as updates expand its offerings.

Let's be real here, both PSO2 classic and NGS are deeply flawed games, with wonky gameplay loops and with development resources often seemingly put in completely arbitrary places. 

Soundtrack? Awesome, top tier even maybe. Great job Sega!
Sound design? What sound design? What the heck Sega, you couldn't even hire your nephew to do a half-assed job?

Combat? Feels genuinely great for an online action RPG, especially NGS. 
Balance? Meaningful decision making in builds? Nah lol just get your skill points and just put them there, you'll have enough.

"Oh cool!" NGS and PSO2 classic shares cosmetics which is objectively awesome!
"Oh..." You have to download BOTH games at the same time for a whopping 100 GB+ storage space, even if you only play one.
"Oh finally!" They finally separated the games! 
"Oh..." But only if you play NGS, if you wanna play PSO2 Classic you still have to download NGS, and even if you only want to play NGS, some of the stuff that was shared between NGS and Classic is now off limits, like music tracks for your jukebox/mag playlist (????????).
 
PSO2 and NGS, even though they happened much later, to me, makes it blatantly clear how awful direction and decision making completely annihilated Sega's place in the console wars. Like you can't BELIEVE Sega was _ever_ Nintendo's number one competitor. 

And yet, goddamn yet, the aesthetics of PSO are just astounding to me, in the best possible way. It has such a specific Sci-Fi vibe that no other game comes even close to emulating, but also it's own unique silliness. The character creation is REALLY good, some of the best if not the best of it's time when classic PSO2 first came out like, 11 years ago or whatever. And while the character creation hasn't had any real major technical updates since then as far as I can tell, it's still really really great, and the sheer amount of continuously added cosmetics more than makes up for whatever shortcomings it may have compared to the cream of the crop nowadays (which I'm pretty sure is just a p*rn game with mods).

I couldn't in good faith recommend either PSO2 Classic OR NGS to an average gamer, it's way too niche, but if you're the kind of person that REVELS in character creation and fashion and can at least tolerate grinding in an online action RPG, these are _the_ games for you, maybe second to none. And even though the game is fundamentally grindy, it really doesn't demand too much time of you, it takes no time at all to do your "important" dailies, but if you decide to stick around for longer than that you'll get even more stuff for it, it's not pointless. 

I also really like the community by the way, both JP and Global. It's pretty clear to me that most people that stick around for this game do so because they genuinely love it, despite its flaws.

Or they just like Sonic too much and can't stand to miss out on all those Sonic events, which admittedly usually are pretty great, and I don't even like Sonic games usually, and I've tried a dozen of them. The current Sonic event is basically comprised of, apart from themed rewards, a singular multiplayer competitive-but-just-for-fun mission where you race seven other players and see who can gather the most points by collecting rings and randomly spawned chaos emeralds which increase your point multiplier, while simultaneously cooperating to clear the stage as fast as possible, with the chance for literally the best and newest loot in the game. Somehow this is literally the most fun Sonic stage of all time, and it just works, it shouldn't, but it does. 

If my hours on record here betrays my credibility, know that I've played PSO2 on and off since the JP release in 2012, I've easily clocked in thousands of hours in total between my OG JP account and my newer global account.

tl;dr: you like cosmetic character customisation? Play. You like weird sci-fi vibes? Play but suspend disbelief. You need any form of consistent game design philosophy and gameplay in your games? Don't play.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Great classic online game with a lot of content but has minor issues.
Rather than say what is great about it, i'll say what isn't as I'm pretty sure plenty of reviews note the good things already.
So I will focus on what might make/break it for some people in rather situational & specific ways.

1. Limited compatibility with lower end pcs due to inability to configure many vital things and no "potato mode"
(While this might seem petty, the base game is crazy old and should run fine on a lower end modern pc but doesn't so it is in fact terribly optimized)

2. A bit convoluted and isn't completely true to the jp version, many things were reworked in negative ways.

3. Dated combat mechanics, it was shortly after we learned we wouldn't get a global version of PSO2 games like tera online released in example which had much higher tier combat quality. The former being 2012 and the latter being 2014, it's safe to say we should be in another league in 2024. Especially considering how hard they try to monetize the title.
(More-so if we consider NGS is like a pseudo pso3 which we might not get for another 10-20 years if ever! The mistake here is a simple underlying factor of not splitting base pso2 from ngs)

4. Steam/epic dependency, this hurts lower end pcs even more and over-complicates getting the game working well. Steam has an astronomical amount of issues and hardly any redeeming factor beyond marketability.

5. Some minor p2w, not purely to the definition of p2w as everything is reasonably achievable by playing. Cashers will undoubtedly have an advantage but it actually doesn't matter much because their gameplay isn't yours. 

If you can look past all of these minor issues and like what you've seen--
You'll have a great time on PSO2, notably I would add if you use an HDD it will cause many issues.
The cheapest upgrades you can perform to get it to run better are:
SDD
Ram modules
Cheap gfx card

Those 3 things can get the oldest junker toasters running it decently but won't fix everything as this game is again very poorly optimized.

As someone who put over 10,000 hours in the Japanese version and currently have XX hours in the NA version, I've got a few things to say.

NEW PLAYERS READ THIS
These are the things you should know right away if you plan to play as a free player with as little trouble as possible
Do NOT feed your mag until you've done your research on how they work
Points in the skill tree cannot be reset without a free reset pass, which is usually handed out often enough as the game updates. But due to the NA version mostly having combat content that JP already has, it's not as often for now. If you have a reset pass feel free to mess around with the class tree to get a feel for things, but if not then you should do your research before putting your points in things you regret. Most of how well your class does depends on how you use these points.
You get 3 characters for free, server-wide. You can put those three characters in one ship, or on different ships.
More characters are your way of making in-game currency, which is how you upgrade your gear and get cosmetics
Don't worry about making your character look perfect on the first try. You can change most things at any time (accessories, eye pattern, tattoos, etc). The things you can't change whenever are things related to the size of the character, shape of their faces, things related to that. But you don't have to worry about that either, because every so often you can obtain a free pass to change your characters looks without paying, and they come often enough. The only thing you can't change at all after making your character is your gender and race.
If you want to avoid paying a cent but want to play every class type, make a character per atk type (Striking, Ranged, Technique)
You can use as many skill discs as you want, there is no limit
Every weapon and unit you pick up is trash, sell it in an NPC shop. Upgrade your gear if it's better. You do not need to hoard them until you start getting 10* drops or better, which in that case you put them in your storage until you learn how to use the recycle shop.
You make money by doing Daily Orders every day, which is located on the left side of the quest gate from an NPC behind a counter. You make the most money by the time you can run things in the Super Hard difficulty. All characters can run them, making them the best way to make money.
Start by talking to Officer Cofy and doing all her client orders, then from there start messing around and have fun!

Now, here are my personal opinions about this game.
I like to describe this game as something like Monster Hunter with Devil May Cry combat. As a free to play MMO, people will approach this with caution. But I'll let you know, this game is very free to play, you can play as well as you desire without paying a single cent. The pay for stuff is mostly for cosmetics and conveniences, to make you in-game money faster through real life money means. But if you know your way around the game, you never have to do this.
Starting out, the game is great! People don't really like to call this an MMO since most quests are only done with up to 12 players in a quest, but who cares. The combat is really fun, the random stuff that occur while going through maps is an experience. Then when emergency quests happen and multiparty bosses appear, those are really fun too! Upgrading gear can be kind of confusing, but isn't hard to do once you talk to others or do your research. It used to be a very frustrating RNG process but not so much anymore.
The only downside is that when you reach endgame, there's sometimes not much to do other than wait for emergency quests to happen and go through your daily CD's (which usually doesn't take too long). Also emergency quests that do not have an objective can be pretty stale, since it's mostly just running around in the circle on a map and one shotting any boss that spawns. A problem can be that bosses aren't all that fun to fight with too many players, since they flinch until dead. But this is mostly fixed later on when harder difficulties are unlocked. Either way though, games combat is too fun to easily put down.
The game is a beautiful anime game, and customizing your character is really great! If you want to make your perfect waifu or mimic a favorite character from a series, it's likely you'll be able to do so in this game. Also, being able to make mech's as well will make the mecha lads pretty happy!
There's talk of censorship but I don't see it. I still have my sexy bikini's, I still can make a character with the fattest and finest tits and ass. When there's cosmetics that pretty much reveals almost all of your characters body, I don't see where the problem is.

Recommended: 55 points over 45.

To leave a fair review of this game and my verdict to recommend it is still a yes, I'll try to keep it simple enough. 
It's not exactly super-different from its -real- (Japanese) counterpart, but here's what I feel. 

The "greater" good: 
-It's mechanically superior to the original for a few hat-tips; for one, it's still cross-play across all its possible platforms, and setting up one's data to connect isn't exactly too difficult. 
-Making payments is easier here as well on each of the platforms (save I can't mention for a basic Windows Store type or Epic Games type, this is coming for the steam version). 
-This version was also the first to have introduced "Mission Pass" mode which gives players prizes for some effort that aren't exactly easy to find, and can add more to where that came from if boosted from Gold Pass. 
-Finally there's the fact that this version is bi-lingual for both JP & EN voices which means there's a few more options (but this has a drawback, will be explained soon.)
-This version has some things somewhat easier on a few cases and have less requirements in some access than the original version; there's currently no "expert" title requirements, so one doesn't have to feel left out if not exactly good enough. 

Naturally, this version however does have drawbacks compared to the real version so not everything is better...

The "worst" bad:
-If someone was a veteran JP version player, be prepared to have to start from ground-zero because your data does not carry over and is not shared. For some who didn't keep an eye on it, you have a lot of work to do... and that won't be fun if you spent a long time in on it. If you didn't start on since the regular 'O2 side, well that stuff will have to be done again, despite both versions of New Genesis (we call "NGS" around here for short) started at the same time but was also the first time when the "real" side isn't exactly easy to get back into anymore. 
-While overtime playershop prices have started getting a nasty inflation of prices vs nice items in the real (JP) version, expect those prices in this version to be multiplied much worse, if not exponentially increased. Good luck trying to get stuff from these "sellers". 
-(My own problem) On the JP side, people are alright with you letting loose to a bit as long as you don't go too far on your appeal, but this version is the exact polar opposite: a stiff-necked community. Accept "parties", "friend requests", or joining "alliances" (teams) carefully at your own risk. Hopefully your experience won't be like mine... 
-While peeps on the real version are somewhat slow on the uptake but eventually get a 40% chance to take down intense Mega-Bosses such as Dark Falz in his Aegis Armor with a very small chance of causing a Meltdown-Kill as well at least, don't expect this version to be able to win; be prepared for high chances of group-wipes, Rangers who don't use Weakener-Bullets on his weak spots to support, or quitters disappearing suddenly. 
-While said: the game is bi-lingual and the male voices are more overall better with few exceptions (for both NPCs and Protagonist boys), the Protagonist girls' voices are subpar to almost downright horrible compared to the real version, and at that note, not every voice was on this version that is in the original either (such as the one I'd like was "censored" as being left out, so I had to have a rough time adapting to a lesser one instead. Subject moot due to mayhap chance future content could possibly bring some in, until then this is a thing.)
-When they said things wouldn't be censored, it was not exactly true. 
-Some complications on other devices half bust the myth that this game is not exactly free, but this version for Steam at least actually is confirmed true. 

Aside of these, most of the game is no different from its real counterpart. My last verdict is 55 over 45 points: Yes. Give it a go, and enjoy the most of it.

Better yet, you can have both a main and a subclass, and up to six different weapons equipped at one time. The elemental system, elemental and physical downs, and the enemy weakpoint and body part breaking system add some depth to the gameplay which leaves it feeling very complete. Overworld enemies do have a bit too much health for my tastes as a solo player but assuming they don't scale with how many people are around I don't mind that too much as it encourages grouping up. I never ran into this problem during the campaign. Ranged does feel extremely strong in comparison to melee, but it does also allow for a sort of difficulty slider where there's clearly some easy classes and some hard ones. The class balance seems great, though I'm no expert from the short time I've actually spent on other classes than Force or Techter. During which I played Gunner, Ranger, and Fighter.

Story is a 6/10, above average, has good moments but the exposition can drag at times and the way it cuts to cutscenes of the battle you just had except you always wield the sword is a tad immersion breaking. Overall though, good concepts, and good story direction, with apt execution.

The cocoons are fun, but I'm sure once you've done them all that's kind of just wrap on those as you've already done them. Once you figure out how to join your friends in their rooms/blocks however the game is very fun to play with friends. 

Monetization, 3/10, gacha. I actually as a person enjoy the heightened rarity of cosmetics as a result of this, but from a consumer standpoint I can't defend gambling. Especially when this game is likely to attract a male teen audience, aka kids.

On face value PSO2 is like waddling into your favorite fast food joint before closing time in your thirties and ordering a supersize combo meal with extra dip and everything on it, a happy meal with the new childhood nostalgia bait toy, and a small diet coke to wash it all down. That's the tagline. 

Really, it's not much of an exaggeration to say that this game should only be played as a fashion sim. It's an all you can eat buffet here when it comes to making your character exactly how you want it to be thanks in large part to SAYGA's unwavering commitment to whoring this franchise out and securing as many collab events as possible to keep the game alive and relevant for it's whales and dwindling player base. Indeed, this game is even better than FFXIV in this regard. But that comes at a steep cost. The trade-off is that everything else in the game is analogous to a diet coke. There's no substance there at all. In fact, it's lackluster and the combat boils down to being just brain-dead tab target spam on repeat. 

But you see, the Phantasy Star franchise itself is a lot like the Chao Gardens in SA2:B but if the Chao's are other people. Yes, it's just a glorified 3D chatroom with an avatar that you can mold into your ideal persona, (you know, how MMO's used to be back in their heyday.) And yes, the combat definitely isn't the main draw, and the quests and story aren't either. But, it's also the interactions with other players that makes Phantasy Star what it is, and what it was. And in that small way, the game is unique enough in a sea of copy pasta MMOs obsessed with bigger numbers to at least install and give a chance. The game doesn't deserve to die in apathy, and who knows, you may make some friends along the way and even get a laugh out of some of the more creative character designs that people came up with. And then as the years speed by and you grow even older you may stop one day and find yourself overcome with a tinge of melancholic nostalgia as you remember the good times you spent in a game that promised you a small glimpse of a fantasy in another world. I know I do.

[h2] Good game to play if you're willing to have your eyes get scarred over with the horrid, abominable, degenerate looks some people have the gall to flaunt in public. [/h2]

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]

The game is really just a standard action RPG where levels don't really matter other than minor stat increments and dictating what gear you can and cannot equip. If you've ever played NieR: Automata, imagine that game but with combat that's about half as complex.

[h3] Content [/h3]

The content of the game is alright for someone starting out, but once you get the story finished and have grinded up to a modern weapon and armors, there's almost nothing worth doing anymore outside of dailies and grabbing regional valuables (a more beneficial and lucrative equivalent of mint collecting for those who know). Lots of players treat this game as a glorified chat room for this reason, and the next topic.

[h3] Phashion and Sunk Cost Fallacy [/h3]

The fashion is absolutely the main pull of this game, and if anyone tells you differently then they need better gameplay standards. The level of character customization in this game is (as far as I know) unmatched in any other games in this genre and of this multiplayer capacity. It's unlikely you'll find yourself dissatisfied unless you have very specific fashion taste, or are looking to cosplay a character whose outfit has no similar analogs in this game.

As you can likely guess, the majority of phashion is locked behind a paywall. You should expect to break out your bank card or do a LOT of grinding (player shop allows paid phashion to be purchased through a grindable in-game currency, but people love to overprice) if you have anything you want that's even remotely popular. Doesn't help that all (even "free") phashion is locked behind a gacha system. 

Most of the aforementioned chat room players are probably only still around because they've spent too much money on the game to bow out now.

[h3] Community [/h3]

This game's community is borderline insufferable at times. I highly suggest any new players start on Ship 1 or 2. I don't know from personal experience but I have heard bad things about ship 3 and 4 folks.

[h2] So, should you play this game? [/h2]

As someone who has spent over 2,500 hours in the PlayStation port, I've thoroughly enjoyed most of my time with the game. I came in with no expectations as someone with no prior experience with the Phantasy Star series, and so wasn't disappointed.

With that being said though, even though I recommend the game, I don't suggest playing it unless you're not susceptible to FOMO, and/or have friends who play. This game is not worth spending money on, but it can be fun.

🎮 Game Experience – Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis Ver. 2
Playing NGS Ver. 2 has been a ride. The revamped visuals and fluid combat caught my eye immediately. I enjoyed exploring the open zones, especially when random events popped up—adds that MMO thrill. I spent time tweaking my character's look (the fashion system is still top-tier), and the photon dash and glide made traversal actually fun.

Combat felt smoother and more responsive compared to the original NGS launch. Whether soloing or partying up for urgent quests, the game kept me engaged, even if the grind can get repetitive. Some of the new creative space features are cool—though they take time to get used to. Met a few chill players along the way too, which definitely helped the experience.

✅ Pros
Massive Visual Upgrade: Gorgeous environments, improved lighting, and character detail really make the world pop.

Smoother Combat: Better responsiveness, more dynamic actions, and cool class synergy.

Open World Freedom: The large open zones and seamless exploration feel liberating.

Character Customization: Deep and stylish—your character can look exactly how you want.

Creative Space: A sandbox-style area to build and design your own zone (like a player housing system with freedom).

Frequent Events & Updates: Keeps things fresh with seasonal content and new gear.

Great for Solo or Party Play: You’re not punished for playing solo, but it’s more fun with others.

❌ Cons
Repetitive Grind: Content loops can get stale—grind for gear, level, repeat.

Sparse Story Content: The narrative can feel thin or stretched out over time.

Performance Issues: Some stutters or load times on older systems or during busy events.

Empty Areas: Sometimes zones feel lifeless unless an event is happening.

UI and Menus: Still a bit clunky and overwhelming, especially for new players.

Gacha System: Fashion and certain upgrades are locked behind scratch tickets and RNG.

Read this if you are from PSO1. I'm strictly talking about Base PSO2 not NGS.

Don't think this is going to be like PSO1. I've got close to 1k hours in PSO1 on Ephinea. PSO1 is much more straight-forward in a lot of ways. Base PSO2 is just not that way. I will try and be as quick to the point about what I have noticed that is different.

The ungodly amount of items that enemies are going to drop is going to overwhelm your psyche and bank.
There are 4 currencies including different types of "passes" that allow you to do things and required for small things that should not be trivial but are. 
There is an ungodly amount of confusing menus.
Multiple exchange shops in the game for different items you obtain.
Some type of grinding of gear and augment. Sacrificing weapons, meseta, and grinders to increase your weapon power. (confusing - I'm level 60 and haven't touched it, haven't had to)
Urgent Quests are actually really cool. Lots of spectacle and fun gameplay there.

I've had more fun playing this game in Solo than Multiplayer. That's because it's difficult to find people your level and then do something together that progresses you through the game (besides leveling). This is because the gameplay can still be really fun without other real people. You can play with other peoples created characters or your own AI companions. I'm not really sure if they do much or not, but they are there.

Mags are nothing like PSO1. Don't even get your hopes up for some fun Mag building and evolving.

Character creation in this game is nothing like I have ever experienced. It's excellent. However, most of the cosmetics are locked behind some type of currency that can involve some type of real money.

I'm lvl 60+ now. I still get overwhelmed by what to do. Crafting is beyond me right now. I'm still kinda mowing through enemies even in solo on Very Hard (even though I can play Super Hard). This game kinda feels like a power-fantasy trip. Where you are mowing down enemies until you take a couple of hits and you're done. (that doesn't feel well-balanced to me).

Challenge mode is in this game. It's fun.

I got kinda overwhelmed with PSO1 when I first started playing. Base PSO2 takes that feeling to a whole new level. In every play session I've had I always get this sick feeling like "there seems to be so much to do, but i don't know what to do".

To me there is so much to do, so many items, so many menus, so much of everything that somehow it leaves me with a feeling of hollowness (sometimes). Paralyzing anxiety about what to do - for sure. I'm doing my best to push through it. If you are familiar with these kinds of systems in a game then it should click with you easier and you'll enjoy it.

A word of warning to every person. Don't mess up your skill tree. You will have to pay money to reset it. Just focus on not screwing that up. Also you'll have a limited amount of hours to customize your character (which i think is a decent amount of time).

In some respects it feels like a natural progression of PSO1. In more ways it feels like it's been tainted by modern convoluted systems. It feels kinda gross if I'm not out fighting something. The nasty tentacles are in here, you see them sometimes, you always feel them.

 I'd still recommend the game, but for me it's like a 6.8/10 when PSO1 is an 8/10 game. PSO2 will not be a classic until a private server pops up that gets rid of a lot of the BS and gives people more freedom to get a hold of customization for their character.

As a beginner, it gets confusing. Tip is to not accept too many tasks when you're in Central City. Another thing is to thoroughly pick your sub class: something you know will suit you and your play style, but don't be afraid to experiment with other classes as you may find something you like. Another tip: don't spend all your gems in one place if you don't plan on spending your money (you don't need to spend money on this game to enjoy it unless you're wanting cosmetics), because the game gives you gems sparingly and you can use those for items that are extremely useful to level up your character.

That's basically all I have to say for me spending nearly 20 hours on this game. I say give it a try yourself.

If you're reading this and want to try the game I'd recommend following these directions: *please note these are my suggestions for how I play, there's no reason to follow this if you'd rather just run around the open world in cute outfits or whatever*

1st- Skip all the cut-scenes and get to max level as fast as possible. Focus solely on the "Main Story" quests and tasks - but don't skip any of the learning!  There will be a little "info window" that pops up with a short description pretty frequently and it's important to read and understand what those are trying to tell you, even if they do a poor job of illustrating the very info they are trying to convey.

(Don't switch classes at first, but do try all the weapons to find the one you want to level first and do the story quests.  You can swap "classes" at any time and having at least one fully leveled will make it a million times easier to swap to any of the other -or all others if you really want- later on)

2nd- You will get free gear as you level as part of leveling a new account, this gear you will use for a long time. I believe it gives you the stuff you will keep at level 65. Current level cap is 100. (3/24/2025)

3rd- Once you hit max level, get your free gear, and finish the story - do all the "cocoons" and "tower" missions to get all of your skill points.  Your "gear score" is what will lock you out of certain missions and you will get some score by *spending* skill points, so make sure you collect and spend all the skill points. There are 47 skill points at present. This will take you approx 15hrs. 

4th- There is a TON of gear and weapons that are "leftovers" from previous expansions and nearly all of them are entirely useless.  Depending on how far into the future you're reading this you'll need to identify "what gear and weapon I should be working on acquiring and improving?"  

At present, the armor is level 10-star and has 3 improvement tiers:
Ektasis - base
Dostasis - 1
Trestasis - 2
Akrotasis - 3 (final at present)

Doing the dailies and weeklies will give you most of the mats you'll need to improve your gear, other things might come from the open world or different challenges, but nothing was hard to find.

At present, the weapons are level 11/12-star and has 3 improvement tiers, with one extra thing to know:
Exelio - base
Duo Selio - 1
Tri Selio - 2
Akroselio - 3
Eredim - (contains a set of 3 unique EX Augments you'll need)

(Ignore Twaalv and Windard type weapons unless you actually roll one - which you won't - at which point just ask someone, lol)

Eredim weapons will always have a group of 3 EX augments which you can transfer to your 
--Selio weapon, but you must always move all 3, no picking and choosing, therefore a set of 3 that compliment one another are more valuable. They offer a bunch of different playstyles so I'll let you figure out which ones you want to use. (I prefer Shortage, Turnover, Maintain Balance if you care to know, I don't recommend it to most players.)

5th- Augments - as you play you'll get augments that you can apply to weapons and gear. Augments that end in "LC" are a weaker variant, but significantly easier to get and apply.  The vast majority of the game can be played and enjoyed with the free gear you'll get at 65, but the "reason to play" if you want to upgrade your gear will be the long tail of getting a set of weapons and armor to upgrade and replacing the augments with stronger and stronger versions as you go.  At the upgrade kiosk you can combine many augments into more powerful ones. These are hard to get and take a lot of time and can be a lot to learn, so take your time.

There are many strategies for augments, preset skills, and weapon potentials.

I don't want to get into the various strategies to do this, but I don't mind farming, so for me - I just bought the base weapons and gear that already had the "Preset Skills" I wanted and went from there to apply the augments I wanted.  Rather than rolling "Preset Skills" after I've already upgraded the weapons and armor.

At present day I have a bit over 400hrs into the game and have a 99.8% complete weapon, and one of the three armor pieces pretty much fully decked out, the other two have LC augments still and one still has a level 4 Preset Skill I'm still deciding what to do with.  I'm providing this information for context in how long it takes if you don't want to just buy stuff with cash, which is also an option for some people.

If you want to buy loot-box cosmetic items and sell them for cash and just buy the best stuff, that is an option if you've got the cash and don't want to care about improving a weapon and gear. Many people do this, I am not one of them.

Notes:

-I do not recommend starting new characters if you can help it.

-Make sure to start on the same server "ship" as your friends.

-If you get two copies of a cosmetic item, the first use will unlock it for your current character, the second use will unlock it for your account.

-Read the challenges and quest information for the dailies and weeklies - don't try to use slam attacks on crit-combo day, for example.

-There's usually not much reason to go crazy and burn yourself out on event tasks, this is maybe the most respectful-of-your-time game that I've ever played considering how easy it is to get enough gear score to do everything and how many "seasonal  points" I've been able to acquire during seasonal events.

-You will make 2 Star Gems (currency) for the first 5 people you "like" their character "lookbook" that resets every day.

-Learn the different shops - there's a lot of info on the page of each shop including how many of each item you can buy each week and how long until the shop resets. There's too many shops and each one has too many items, just take your time.

-There's a yellow "treasure" item in each zone that always spawns at the same spot each day that gives a decent amount of money. It takes less than 10 minutes to get all of them each day once you have the teleports to each zone.

-The grinding zones (Dext Base for money for example) have different levels based at what level your character is. You can select the different levels at the teleporters on the map for each zone. Do this for different drops, money, xp, or whatever you're looking for. Usually, for money you'll want the lower levels for higher total kills, for xp you'll usually want the higher levels for more exp per kill.

Good luck on killing Ruine Masquerader at level 100!

the only things I really hated about base pso2 was the obtuse and unnecessarily complicated affixing system, and the gazillion types of currencies. NGS solved those and also brought shiny new graphics and an open world, but at what cost? pretty much everything else. what used to be a more customizeable and varied combat experience is now so watered down that all classes feel almost the same. gone are the highly varied and epic boss designs and fight mechanics (except maybe the dark falz and retem worm). the monsters are all same-y not just in aesthetics, but in mechanics as well. Base PSO2 had the many Dark Falz's, Red Dragon, Masquerade, Yamato, AIS space fight, ep6 final boss, all accompanied by the epic scenarios, all play very differently from each other. 
NGS profoundly (hehe) confuses me. PSO2 was already great! all it needed was some trimming of abandoned features and reworking the affixing system, i think. ok, new combat mechanics, open world, new story, cool! why not a full sequel instead? maybe they wanted to carry over the loads of cosmetics, tie them together and stuff, maybe a way to cover the licensing issues with the collabs idk? a way to reuse the assets and save workload? but they still had to remaster all those anyway???? ok, maybe just the idea of having all your stuff from base onto a new world is cool. i think it is. but then it effectively kills the player market for base PSO2?? was base PSO2 really meant to be left alone and abandoned?? Why even join them in the first place?????

I could probably go on forever on all the stuff that Base PSO2 had that just got lost in NGS for forever and all the other questionable decisions put into the game, but at this point, it's all been said by others.

----------------------

WHY THE RECOMMENDATION:
Now, all that are negatives and just me ranting my disappointment on what the game has become and how base PSO2 was meaninglessly killed off. So why the recommend?

well, taking for what the game is, NGS is, well, fine. It has solid gameplay in its foundation. there's a sizeable amount of content to enjoy. It's not objectively "bad" per se, it's still pretty fun to play for a while actually! If you're a newcomer, I recommend playing it with a few friends casually. Base PSO2 is still also technically playable too and it's pretty good for what it is. It's got the advanced classes and infinitely better boss encounters, although of course it's also a decade old game, so expect it to feel rather bloated/overwhelming for a while.

as a veteran player though, I just.. I'm never playing this game again. NGS, what it's become and becoming, the death of base pso2... there's just too much heartbreak and disappointment for me now. most of the things i really liked just arent in NGS anymore. and they dont seem to be coming back either. Maybe if the Etoile class comes back and we get more bosses as fun as those i mentioned, I'll reconsider it. idk. I'm really just a pso2 boomer now i guess.

PSO2NGS is, in many ways, inferior to PSO2. This is because the game's direction is that there is no direction. The open world idea is great and all, but it plays more like a mode that would be attached to PSO2 than anything else. The core identity of PSO2 was the drop-in play and the quest lobbies. PSO2 was effectively an arcade game, which makes sense on why it had a couple of SEGA arcade collaborations. You drop in, play as much as you want, call it a day. Get loot, grind levels, so on. The idea of loot and power kept changing for the worst, unfortunately, and applies to PSO2 as a whole. 

How many f'ing stars will you add to your rarity before it's enough? 13 star items? Oh, now it turns out that 15 stars make 13 stars garbage.
... Of course, that's not the actual problem. The problem is that these stars are tied to time-gated events. PSO2 is basically what'll happen to NGS in terms of equipment.

The NGS story is set 1000 years later, but, APPARENTLY... ARKS fell during half that time.
Spoilers? Hardly. This is necessary knoweldge.
THE ARKS. You're telling me the ARKS, SET UP TO SAVE LIFEFORMS FROM EXTINCTION, FELL? We, the player character that happens to harness the power of Dark Falz a la DARK BLAST, was powerless on a new threat. The AIS against the Magatsu, the evolution of technology and the riders, the third/fourth/fifth new power that was Episode 6 in a nutshell.

All of that, for what?

Whoever the F was behind the story made PSO2NGS completely irrelevant as a story. There's no point in following it, and should be seen as an nonclinical what-if OR one of those alternate story-line generations from PSO2 EP6. ARKS is an acronym. Artificial Relict to Keep Species.
Now? 

We're conveniently, Artificial Relict to Keep Species Defenders. Yep. 'They' forgot their own acronym. 

The story content itself didn't matter, the overall story and idea was enough. PSO2 was about having a passable story, NGS is about trying to reset the legacy but unable to committing to a new game entirely. The original idea was nice, having both games run along each other and sharing data and even some items.

PSO2 was actually full of interesting ideas; when they added the fourth race... which was the same models as others but with a horn sticking out and other minor differences... they at least redid the opening and gave it a reasonable time/sci-fi explanation.

I actually have zero interest in NGS's story knowing that everything we did in PSO2 was worth less than nothing.
Unfortunately, it also made PSO2's story kind of worthless to invest in. The PSO2's Episode Oracle anime is good enough as a watchable summary. EP4 is mediocre, and 5 and 6 are enjoyable/whatever, if you can get to that point without burning out.

================
As an Open World, NGS has all the trademark garbage associated with it. Trash mobs that give next to no EXP, the ability to walk into enemies twice your level, and nothing rewarding. Shrines, a la BOTW, exist for Skill Points and other such. Why? How? Old MMOs actually let you grind in open fields with enemies that give EXP and drops.

The only plus is Ccombat is okay. Unfortunately, the basic idea for it is turning all base classes into PSO2's 'Scion' classes. PSO2's biggest problem was that the Scion classes ruined the game through high DPS, locking players into only a few choices once unlocked. They were the concept that became the gateway to NGS and why NGS plays quite differently. Thanks, team behind 'Scion'.

PSO2 itself is difficult to truly min/max in, as they locked all the speed leveling and gearing options away through time limits. Instead of having a repeating rotating cycle to still drop items, they decided to leave it with nothing.

Now, Both PSO2 and NGS (which people keep forgetting, it's not "base pso2", it's PSO2 & NGS), still contain some goodness to it, which is why I can still say it's okay to exist.

The character creator leads to creativity and fun creations, even though the pieces are likely absurdly expensive, and a few are even race-locked between CAST and fleshlings. It's still a great dress-up simulator with some fun combat.

PSO2 can still be played in 'Solo' mode, or rather, playable alone. The core of it shows that it's a game that can eventually be re-worked for a console offline version with peer-2-peer connectivity to keep it alive forever. (Even though we know SEGA will drop it once it ded.)

NGS, on the other hand, feels more like it is played alone due to the open structure. I know there are drastic differences between JP and US, such as economy, making NGS much more playable in Japan due to player economy alone.

PSO2 itself is still quite fun and still a unique experience, while NGS feels less new. PSO2 was about hitting big numbers in 'normal' amounts, depending on PA and class anyways, while NGS is hitting smaller numbers in big amounts, regardless of class choice.

While it'll take me a while to come to terms with NGS and like it, all the negativity stems from what people actually liked about PSO2 and now NGS gets all of those things wrong. NGS is basically the corporate version of PSO2. PSO2 was crafted with love, and players loved it from all over the world, even though it was in Japan for 8 years.

NGS is by no means 'bad', it's just... wrong. It's PSO2 gone wrong. It needs a FF14-styled revamp to give it it's identity back.
Sure, quests exist, but it's different in that they're only for a few specific things. Sure, Photon Arts exist, but that's also different.

Also, the terminally online troglodytes that can't be banned because they spend lots of money. That's a huge negative.
Seriously, the perpetually horny plebs who, for whatever reason, can't bring themselves to masturbate and get it out of their system, need to take it online and make it their entire identity. An issue in all forms of PSO2, including JP servers. They can be blacklisted to ignore, but the Symbol Arts stay in the cache.

It sucks, though, to see all these new enemies effectively be old reskins. I thought 'Sadinian?!' the moment I saw the "Pettas Sword". Why are there so many old enemies on this new planet? I might've missed the answer somewhere, or there isn't an answer. Regardless, I give NGS a solid half score, while PSO2 is a solid '7'. The core of PSO2 still exists and how it plays is still 'classic'. A good new game for free, should someone need something fresh without paying a cent.

But, SEGA is stupid as all hells, and that PSO2 is a separate DLC that is required to download alongside NGS IF you want to play classic PSO2 and not new NGS. That type of decision is why NGS is chock full of issues that frustrate long-time players and former PSO2 fanatics.

All said and done, if you're in the first world and can do the download, it's worth a try.

I mean, after all, they're both still free games, and NGS didn't shut PSO2 down directly. For a free game, it's quite surprising, and if you factor in the many years of love PSO2 had, it's a complete game available for free. Limitations apply here and there, but really, there's not much to lose if you're unable to pay for anything else.

[h1]This is a review of New Genesis. Not base PSO2. The games [b]ARE DIFFERENT.[/b][/h1]

TLDR: Great if you like games like genshin or JRPGS like nier automata/ xenoblade chronicles.

[h2]Goods:[/h2]
The game has one of the best character creators of any game I've ever played. 

Mechanically, the game feels amazing, very satisfying to beat enemies and level up.

The community while small, is overall quite friendly. Definitely an extroverts game.

For an MMORPG the game looks modern, good HDR support and support for FSR and DLSS.

An incredible level of customization for your character and "most" items can be obtained without money.

The game is truly free to play with no combat restrictions for players who don't want to spend.

[h2]Mids:[/h2]
The game definitely is hard to grind for long times. Most of the activities are daily and are reshuffled on Tuesdays, so it can get a little stale by the end of the week.

The game isn't particularly difficult and the story isn't finished. If you're looking for a competitive experience this really isn't a game for you. 

Crashing isn't uncommon, usually referred to in the community as "getting SEGA'D" personally has happened to me 3 times in the 250 hours I've played. However I've lost 0 progress to it, so it's not too big of a deal.

Most of the game really starts once you get level 75, while this isn't too hard to get given how fast you level up, the community of the game doesn't really exist at the lower levels. 

The game plays its BEST with an alliance/friends. This game is rather boring alone. If you are someone who doesn't like interacting with other players this game will feel hollow and boring.

[h2]Bads:[/h2]
This game does have a lot of paid content. Most if not all of it is cosmetic but if you want your character to look its best you kind of do have to spend real money due to the second issue of this game.

The player economy is VERY inflated. most of the popular or cutest items are near impossible to grind for simply due to the ridiculous price tag on everything. For a quick reference, doing all of your daily quests will give you 100,000 of the ingame currency called Meseta, small cosmetics like wings, hats, and special outfits can easily cost 10-30 million Meseta. Of course not all outfits cost that much, however thats a good idea of the kind of economy exists in the game.

This game is also a weeb game, not that that's a bad thing. It's just that if you're coming from something like WoW or other MMORPGs this game will feel odd with the amount of skin you're allowed to show and the overall nature of the game/community.

[h2] Overall Thoughts [/h2]
I love this game. It has brought me countless hours of fun and gave me so many fun memories and wonderful friends. However, this game isn't going to be for everyone. If you enjoy customizing your character exactly how you want and showing off your fashion talents or even home designing skills in front of people, this game is for you. If you are looking for a deep story experience with loads of solo content, this game is not for you. It's probably my favorite MMORPG I've ever played, but definitely flawed.

Short Review: 
Yes. Get this. The worst that can happen is maybe you don't fall in love right away, there's no real lose here. 10/10 

Longer Review:
PSO2 NGS is one of the coolest games in general and it's even more impressive considering it's an MMO. I have a limited history with the series, starting with PSO2 base before the global launch, playing on the Japanese servers. It wass a long time ago, but I was really addicted to it. It had actually fallen off my radar, though, and I missed the global release, not realizing it was a thing until NGS. I tried it then and it seemed okay, but there wasn't a TON to do then, not as much as before, anyway. That is no longer the case.

My friends and I were looking for something to do after coming off of FFXIV. For us, Eorzea had lost its appeal and we wanted to try to find something, anything, to fill the gap it left. On a whim, I decided to give NGS a shot and after a night of streaming some of it, everyone was on board and we have been daily junkies for this since. There is a lot to talk about here, and I'll try to keep my thoughts organized and brief. 

Story - As anyone who tried FFXIV might relate to, good story isn't all that common in MMOs. NGS doesn't care about that trope and crafts an interesting story that keeps itself grounded and real, produces interesting characters that go through powerful arcs, and even functions to provide lore reasons for gameplay mechanics. It is hard to discuss without spoiling later parts, but as someone who likes to poke fun at things like "well this is obviously because it's a game," I found the answers they eventual reveal to be very satisfying.

The basic plot involves the player character and gives a sense of importance without falling into the pitfalls of a "chosen one" affair that can often give a feeling of disconnect between story and regular MMO life. Progression feels natural, but it also doesn't waste a lot of time. A power player can rush through the whole thing relatively quickly. It's great for those who care about story and not a huge barrier for those who don't. 

Gameplay - NGS has a lot of style and flash in its combat, but it also has the substance to back it up. The controls are solid and movement is fun. It may seem like a lot at first, and it definitely can be, but even if you don't pick up playstyles quickly, the end game content is still accessible.

Combos are done more similarly to an action game rather than a traditional MMORPG, using a variety of moves to pull off complex attacks. Spells and the like can be charged by holding down a button rather than waiting on a timer. Dodging feels great and parrying, while harder to perfect, is extremely potent and fulfilling. Fights are also a lot of fun, with bosses using a set group of attacks in a random order across various phases. The added platforming during really keeps you on your toes!

Music - A+++. It's Sega. This is their thing. The entire soundtrack is so great, even the simple things. 

Graphics - For a game built on top of an older game, NGS is extremely gorgeous. The colors are so vibrant, the landscapes breathtaking. There are particle effects all over and the lighting is divine. That all said, if you don't have the best machine, it still runs great on lower settings while not sacrificing the spirit of the higher end visuals.

Other stuff that I don't know how to categorize - There has been controversy with this game and some people aren't thrilled with Sega, so I want to take a second to talk to those issues. NGS took the place of the original Phantasy Star Online 2 and having experienced some of the best that game had to offer, I completely get it. A lot of what PSO2 was isn't in NGS, but there is still a lot of love and passion and even humility to be felt from the developers. They are working on building something great with little updates coming constantly and larger ones spread out a bit more. Compared to other major games in the MMO field, NGS is getting a ton of attention and care from the people working on it. I don't want to drag other things here, but if you know, you know. If you don't, lucky you, I hope you realize how good you are eating!

There is also the concern of Gacha elements. Yes, you can buy in-game currency to get special random ticket items for fashion. Yes, it's not as straight forward as picking something from a catalogue and ordering it. However, with how the game's economy works, it is not that big of an issue. First, AC (in-game currency) is entirely optional and not needed to play the game in its entirity. You never have to spend a penny here if you don't want to. And that brings me to the second point, which is personal shops. The same items that you can pay to get tickets for can be sold and purchased on shops run by players. A free to play player can grind to buy from another player, and those who pay and don't get what they want can resell and purchase something they do. All games monetize in some way or another, and considering how much here is just given away and how the Gacha has workarounds, this is probably the least predatory monetization I've ever seen in an MMO. 

Oh, yeah, and the housing is absolutely bonkers good.

tl;dr: The game has its flaws yet I can't stop playing it. Fun (but repetitive) gameplay with great customisation. 

Few games let premium features be accessible to free-to-players, but in this case, SEGA has shown some generosity.
There are numerous ways of getting the Star Gems currency to access things like the premium battlepass and renting extra storage space for materials. If you're a new player, I'd advise saving the Star Gems on Material Storage Rental, your inventories can get cluttered quick, having a button to deposit the crafting materials all at once in the storage is handy.

My biggest gripe so far is that character slots are limited unless you are willing to spend real money, and I'm the kind of person that likes having multiple different characters/styles for roleplaying. You can somewhat work around this by having set "looks" be bookmarked for easy switching between several styles. There are also salon passes and color passes which are trivial to obtain, so you're free to experiment as much as you like. I also wish performance was just a little better, it takes a painful amount of time to log in and loading into new regions can get tiresome with how often/long the game halts. With that said, apparently performance was in a worse state before I got in, so I suppose I should be thankful the game runs at all.

Core gameplay is very fun and engaging with parries and dodging, however it can also be repetitive, especially so when seeing the same enemies you've fought in the tutorial still lurking around far later into the game. The small amount of the special moves that the weapons are provided doesn't help with this problem either. The toolkit you get is the toolkit you will have for the rest of the game, except you may get an extra whistle or two to shake up the gameplan, e.g: A counter attack when you dodge an attack, or you unlock a meter to build up with attacks that can be spent on a heavy hitting attack. 

The amount of customisation and options at the player's disposal can be overwhelming and that's a good thing, there is so much to experiment with and sink your teeth into here. However you will also have to work for your drip, auction house prices are high and you'll have to work on your dailies/weeklies to earn enough for the gear you want. With that said there's also a free gacha accessible every day alongside a gacha accesible via star gems.
It's alright, I guess.

So i feel like I'm probably a good candidate for a review as I played PSO Episodes 1+2 plus for both Xbox and GameCube, both offline and online. And I had an absolute blast playing those. I then went on to CARD and somehow even enjoyed that, followed by PSU. I've enjoyed every PSO game I've played because simply put. It's formula.  The gameplay has been historically simple and enjoyable for the most part, the elements associated with the plot and story lines have also made for pleasant and heartwarming experience. 

The reason I say this is because PSO2 and PSO2 NGS I feel are more appealing as games for previously established fans of the genre... PSO 2 took what made PSO and PSU successful and implemented those same mechanics, with an introduction of various new features.. such as a slew of more fashion oriented items, a system where you can upgrade weapons and armor and even other various features such as customizable techniques, photon arts, class leveling and more. That said, as a fan of the old stuff, these are awesome upgrades and implementations and definetely add to the richness and enjoyment level of the game and I haven't even touched upon aspects such as clans and player shops. 

NGS took what made PSO2 successful and followed that same style of formulaic upgrading, except now we got a serious graphical overhaul, an open world and a level of richness never before seen in a PSO game. In fact it's so rich that to new players it can be overwhelming! And there in lies the problem I feel new players will struggle with. 

This game seems like a game that you can just pick up and play on the surface (and it is) but there is a learning curve. In PSO2 and NGS there is more tact necessary during combat, you have to learn how things work in order to properly specialize your character, you need to learn how the armour and item systems work over time in order to properly maximize your fighting potential, as with any RPG. But once you do learn those mechanics (which can be done within 5-10 hours of gameplay easily) you really start to appreciate its charm and creativity. There's a lot of life in it, a lot of passion. You get a sense the developers really did try to make a good, enjoyable game. 

And most of all, the game is free. You can spend money on the premium set (and various other cosmetic items) and doing so really does add an even deeper level of richness into the game regarding the quality of life experience (more rewards for your time, expanded storage, access to player-based economy) but the cool thing is you can access this stuff as a free player as well in limited time usage increments, so you can get a taste for it and see if its worth it to you before electing to spend the $13 for 30 days of premium play. Often times there's also sales as well, I currently am utilizing 30 days of premium play for just $5. 

In reality, its a good game. It's free, its fun. Don't be afraid to join a clan and play the main story too. It really helps smooth things out and prep you to be at a solid level to join other players for endgame. Seasoned RPG veterans could grind through it in easily 10-15 hours. In a world where games are commonly feeling like half-finished cash grabs it does feel as if PSO has more respect for your time and wallet. And the nostalgia factor hits hard as well (in case you couldn't tell) 

All in all, I say to fans of the genre and newcomers alike. Give it a chance! It's a lot of fun!

[h1] A Tale of Two Halves: Phantasy Star Online 2 vs. New Genesis [/h1]
Phantasy Star Online 2 (PSO2) and its successor, New Genesis, represent contrasting chapters in the iconic Phantasy Star franchise. While PSO2 has garnered praise for its rich content and engaging gameplay, New Genesis has faced criticism for what some perceive as a lackluster experience. Let's delve into the strengths and weaknesses of each to provide a balanced perspective.

[h3] Phantasy Star Online 2 - The Classic Jewel [/h3]
Phantasy Star Online 2 has been celebrated for its longevity, having sustained a dedicated player base since its initial release. The game's strength lies in its extensive content, featuring a plethora of diverse quests, challenging raids, and an intricate narrative that unfolds across various episodes. The combat system is dynamic and responsive, offering players a satisfying blend of strategy and action. Moreover, the character customization options and the variety of classes contribute to a deeply immersive gaming experience.

The game's graphics, while not cutting-edge, have aged well, maintaining a charming aesthetic that complements the sci-fi fantasy setting. The developers have consistently supported PSO2 with regular updates, events, and collaborations, ensuring that players always have something new to explore.

[h3] New Genesis - A Promising Concept, But Falling Short [/h3]
On the other hand, Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis has been met with mixed reviews, with many players expressing disappointment in various aspects. While the open-world concept brought a breath of fresh air, the execution left much to be desired. The game's visuals, though improved, have not matched the expectations set by contemporary standards, resulting in an experience that feels underwhelming compared to other titles in the genre.

The transition to a more action-oriented combat system in New Genesis was meant to enhance gameplay, but for some, it has led to a loss of the strategic depth that characterized PSO2. Additionally, the removal of traditional classes and the introduction of a skill tree system have polarized the community, with some applauding the flexibility and others lamenting the loss of class identity.

Furthermore, server stability issues and a perceived lack of endgame content at launch contributed to a rocky start for New Genesis, leaving players yearning for the depth and polish that defined its predecessor.

[h3] Conclusion [/h3]
In the world of Phantasy Star, the tale of PSO2 and New Genesis unfolds as a nuanced narrative. Phantasy Star Online 2 stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of its formula, with its wealth of content, engaging gameplay, and vibrant community. On the other hand, New Genesis, while introducing ambitious concepts, has struggled to live up to the legacy of its predecessor, facing criticism for technical issues and design choices that have left players wanting more.

[b]• ULTIMATELY[/b], the appreciation for each title hinges on individual preferences. Some may find solace in the familiar embrace of PSO2, while others may see the potential for improvement in New Genesis as it evolves with future updates and adjustments. Only time will tell whether New Genesis can carve out its own space in the Phantasy Star universe or if it will forever live in the shadow of its predecessor

(This is a review of NGS and not base PSO2. I clarify this because both titles are included in this game, and you can carry your characters cosmetics over between games, but NGS is the game I have played more.)

This is a really fun game to play casually. If you want a game that has good-feeling combat and top-notch character customisation, I would absolutely check this game out.

While it isn't the most complicated in the world, the combat feels great. The animations are cool, and the parry and cancel windows are well-tuned, so it feels very easy to be in control of the action. This might be the best action gameplay I've ever seen in an MMO.

The game focuses a lot of parrying attacks and most classes have some mechanic that makes it beneficial to just stand in front of an enemy and try to max your DPS while parrying all their attacks. That feels amazing to do, but it can make all the classes feel a bit samey. However, different classes have different mechanics that sit on top of and parallel to that loop, so you still have some options. I would recommend playing a handful of classes so you can switch it up when you've had enough of one class.

Really trying to min-max this game can be a struggle. The drop rates for best-in-slot gear (and let's be honest, second-best-in-slot gear) can be downright abysmal. However, if you don't love the grind, you simply don't have to play that way. The game is not so hard that you need the best of the best, and there are always pretty accessible options for mid range gear that will be completely serviceable for the game. You can choose how hard to go on this game.

In my opinion, the character customisation is [b]best-in-class[/b]. It doesn't feel like "fashion is endgame" or "your character has to look bad for 200 hundred hours" as is seemingly the mantra of many other MMOs. Even though the gacha for cosmetics is the biggest driver of in-app purchases, they are very forthcoming with good cosmetics for F2P players, and it's not too hard to save up and buy items you want from the player shop. You might not get everything you want, but you will be able to get good stuff and make a sick-looking character.

On that note, I actually feel like this game is very fair for F2P players. Even though selling on the player shop and getting extra storage are technically paid features, there are reliable methods of getting access to these features. Again, you can't have everything for free, but you're definitely going to have everything you need.

Another aspect of customisation is this really awesome feature called creative space. You get a plot of land and can build basically whatever you want on it. Players can make houses or gardens or design little games; really you can do whatever. It's a lot of fun. You get a special currency every day for visiting other players' creative spaces, so you are incentivized to check out what people have made. I have sunk SO much time into building my creative space and exploring other peoples' spaces. I do wish there was a stronger culture in the playerbase of hanging out and chatting in creative spaces, but it's still neat as-is.

The story is kind of meh. There are some nice cutscenes and near the end of the first episode, things really start picking up, but you will probably work through the existing story pretty quickly and not be too blown away. It isn't bad though, and there's room for things to open up, I hope.

That brings me to breadth of content. The development of this game, including story content drops, has been quite slow and it felt sparse for a long while. According to the devs, it took them a long time to even get to where they wanted to be at launch Things are getting a bit better, though. In the last year they've added some genuinely fun bosses and game modes and they often run limited time quests that give you something new to try out pretty regularly.

But, I have to say, there isn't TONS of content. Plus, not all content has good drops past a certain point, so it can feel like there is even less viable content. It seems like the team is getting smarter about how they make content and structure rewards, but keep in the mind that there's not a super deep backlog of stuff to do.

Overall, I think the core of the game is incredible. It's easily one of my favourite games ever. But, the breadth of content and drop rates are gonna bother you if you try to no-life this game. That's why I say it's an amazing game to play casually. Whether that means regularly playing a little bit here and there, or binging it for a few weeks every couple months, I wholeheartedly recommending installing this game and trying it out ASAP.

Overall, PSO2NGS is a great game for anime/manga fans. Here's my review:

Story - This game is catered to anime fans of course, and the story is.. well.. decent. Not the best anime story in a game, but also not the worst. At certain parts of the story campaign it drags on and on to the point you will want to skip through dialog. Just like a lot of anime stories, it tends to over-explain things, which just increases the dialog time and decreases the play time. I noticed myself getting bored with the story about midway through. Your mileage may vary. But who really plays these kinds of games for the story anyway?

Classes - This is one of the things I love most about PSO2NGS. Classes are diverse and most offer a variety of weapons so you aren't stuck using the same weapon the whole time. You also have the option to have a Sub-Class, which is nice because you get the benefits of that classes abilities/buffs as well as your main class's. And it allows you to use another set of weapons, increasing your options. What's even better is that you can completely change up your class and sub-class anytime you like! So you'll never get bored with your fighting style. There are multiple options for melee, mid range, and long range fighting styles depending on your class as well. So you can find the perfect combo of class and sub-class to fit your playing style.

Style - This game is FILLED with style options, and everything can be had for free! Yes, there are AC scratch tickets that require real money to use, but most of the items end up in the game's marketplace for free.. of course some items are priced for ridiculous amounts of gold.. so you'll need to farm a lot of gold to go the free route. I absolutely love the style in this game tho. You can, if you choose, just spend all your time playing dress up if you like.. "forget the monsters, I want to focus on fashion today! n.n" PSO2NGS also offers a lookbook system that allows you to save your outfits and share them with the community. The fashion scene is pretty big in this game, and for good reason!

Customize-ability of Characters - You have a bunch of options here as well. You can spend hours in the salon changing just about ever aspect of your character. No 2 PSO2NGS characters are alike, unless it's on purpose lulz. There is no standard avatar or anything like that. You can generally choose from a few different body types and head shapes, and then you can customize them with sliders/graphs to your heart's content. You could even put male heads on female bodies or vice versa if that's your thing! (eww). Eye color, hairstyles, color, body shape, etc can all be changed at anytime with the use of salon passes or star gems. When you first start out, salon passes may be few and far between, ,but don't worry, overtime you'll collect quite a few from just playing the game and receiving campaign items from Sega. N-color change passes allow you to change the colors of clothing, which you will also collect and stack up over time for free.

End Game - So once you finish the story there isn't a whole lot to do other than daily tasks, hang with friends, create fashion, try new weapons, classes, build up your weapons and armor, collect titles, collect animations such as dances and poses and idles... yeah.. there's a lot to still do in the game lulz. You can run triggers, leciel, nameless city, etc as well if you need dungeon type content to do. But generally for me I do my daily tasks, work on my outfits, and chat/hangout and/or shop the marketplace for new clothes/hair/accessories/animations. End game in PSO2NGS can be as chill as you like, or as grindy as you like. You just need to understand your options. Most of the time just doing your daily tasks and alliance tasks is enough to keep you busy for a bit as well as to earn you gold and free scratch tickets. Sega introduces new Limited Time Quests as well that offer special rewards mostly every week. And since I have been playing, there has always been some kind of festival with special tasks to do until the last couple weeks where one just ended. 

TLDR - Give this game a try if you like anime style games, fashion, farming, and chatting. PSO2NGS has a lot to offer just about everyone. And if you get bored with NGS, you can always go and play PSO2.. the original version of the game. It's not bad despite being old. Bottom line is, you're not going to know if you like this game or not until you give it a try. And if you feel lost, feel free to ask the community for help. Most people are very nice and helpful, and there is also a healthy YouTube community to help you improve and learn the game. But don't feel pressured to grind this game, take you time and just enjoy it for what it is.

I have about 600 hours on PS4.

The people in charge of this game clearly do not see it as anything more than a means to fleece people out of their money. All other content -- story, combat, character building -- comes secondary to new gacha banners. Even the new Creative Space feature, while admittedly pretty in-depth, is just another way for them to nickel and dime you with cosmetic fluff.

It's been month after month of recycled content and reskinned enemies, and they've outright said they have no plans for anything more. Story updates are a joke, you wait four months for one five minute cutscene in which the characters talk at each other with those canned "stand there blankly staring and maybe waving my arms" talking animations. Your character is able to interject in the conversation exactly two times per cutscene, no more and no less. You only ever get two dialogue options, and they're often just the same sentence worded in different ways. Absolutely nothing cool ever happens in these cutscenes, because they are so short and so cheaply animated that there's literally nothing they CAN do.

The open world is kind of pretty, but has nothing to do in it outside the hub cities -- there are no small towns, NPCs, or side quests out there -- so there's little incentive to actually go out and explore. There are repeatable dungeons you can run, but the rewards are either vendor trash or outdated, so they're all completely dead zones. 

Combat is fluid, responsive, and feels good, but there is almost no variety in character classes. Everyone is just a different flavor of damage, with the few support abilities being Ranger's Blight Rounds and Techter's ONE party buff. If you try to build your character in any way other than maximum DPS, you're making them worse.

The character creator is pretty extensive and there is some fun to be had with it. It's possible to make a character that looks cool without spending any real money as long as you're willing to grind. However, the declining playerbase means fewer people are playing the gacha, which means less stuff in the personal shops, which means prices get inflated to obscene levels and are only increasing with time. They playerbase itself seems to be a lot younger than me and I don't interact at all.

I genuinely think this could be a good game if they put a lot of work into it, but it desperately needs some people in charge who actually play the game themselves and care about making something fun, instead of just cynically preying on the wallets of nerdy dudes trying to build their waifu
