I had 250 hours in this game on the US release, playing via the Windows Store here in the UK long before it officially came to the EU. At the start, it felt like a true sequel to Phantasy Star Online and Phantasy Star Universe. The gameplay was fun, the setting familiar, and for a brief moment, it looked like SEGA understood what made the older games special.

I was a huge fan of PSO1 and PSU—despite having nearly zero interest in anime or traditional JRPGs (I like a few select animes and jRPG games) What drew me in wasn’t flashy visuals or cliché character tropes, but the grounded, lonely sci-fi atmosphere. Those games had a sense of mystery, isolation, and quiet discovery. Storytelling came through ruins, data logs, and strange anomalies that made the world feel lived-in and eerie. They respected the player's intelligence and let the environment tell the tale. It was subtle, immersive, and truly unique for its time.

Then came PSO2, and it all went downhill.

Somewhere along the line, SEGA decided to cater almost entirely to the weeb crowd. I don't mean your average anime enjoyer, i mean the other kind. The game quickly devolved into a fanservice circus—anime girls in absurdly skimpy outfits, physics-defying "milkers," and an endless flood of immersion-breaking cosmetics that have no place in a sci-fi setting. Every corner of the game became infected with over-the-top cringe, and the atmosphere that once set this series apart was drowned out by loud, flashy nonsense and tone-deaf character spam.

The community? Just take one look at the Steam hub or any social space in-game—it's wall-to-wall gooner bait and terminally online degeneracy. It's not just disappointing; it's embarrassing. Again, its not standard anime tropes they have focused on as i can kinda get into that. They've gone so far into the gooner side of weeb culture its beyond saving. That's whats ruining the game. 

SEGA took a franchise that once stood proudly apart from typical JRPG fluff and sacrificed it for shallow appeal and monetised cosplay. They killed what was once my first MMO experience on the Dreamcast, and what could have been a masterpiece successor became a gaudy mess. PSO2 might still have decent combat and core mechanics buried somewhere underneath, but it's completely unrecognisable as a Phantasy Star game in spirit.

I took a hiatus that was planned to be quitting this game if I found nothing of interest nor change to dynamics that would bring me back.

Update 2.0 adds base building. I'm happy with the addition, but as per usual the UI and menu flows in the game are just horribly clunky. There are things I wish I could change colors on, if not select from some textures, but can't -the typical issues I have with character items as well where for certain items what can be changed isn't enough to make thinks look matching with other items.


I can't even sell anything I have extra for in-game currency because the market to sell anything to other players is locked behind a paywall, so I either scrap it like getting 5 cents back on an aluminum can or it stays in storage.

Gameplay takes a while to get better where AI start to be a challenge to a rifle user (the recommended choice for solo play), and yet really the only way to put me in peril that the AI has is numbers and filling gaps in the attack of one type with the attack of another unit type.

A lot of the cut scenes are clunky and not smooth -plenty of big gaps between character dialog. I'm sorry to say the VA and model movements often aren't in proper sync. A lot of the enemies can't hit me to save themselves and the team behind this game seem to want to push constant rewards where you get shields and weapons that break the initial progression grind of the game (already boosted and with augments and hidden ability level). It seems they really want you to speed through the content to end game so you are left with the customization aspect and maybe dump money on buying AC to do premium pack purchases or roll the gatcha wheel (which is disguised as scratch tickets).

I believe I had about 40 hours on PS4 that aren't logged over here.

I still refuse to recommend this game -if you don't have people to play with and are not into seeking people out.

That said, even though I don't recommend it, there are those who may like it. It has been stable the entire time thus far and I've played far worse games. The issue is all in how it makes me feel playing it, clunky gameplay experiences, and that it can't seem to respect itself as being a game and yet fails to want to go all in on being some weird social app with deeply customize-able characters (which is also clunky) and yet also the main source of revenue for the game. In fact, it introduced a plethora of issues, such as skill points being tied to BOTW-esque trials, loot feeling inconsequential, and all classes lacking any identity. The latter might be the worst bit considering how PSO (and even PSU) managed to cultivate the identity of its classes up until later in PSO2's life cycle. And no, the open-world is not even remotely fun to explore. It's fun to traverse, but there's nothing about it that justifies its existence.

All in all, NGS is an absurdly dumbed down game that focuses primarily on cosmetics rather than the loot rush that made this franchise special for 20 years. It's sad that SEGA decided to chase industry trends instead of sticking to what makes PSO what it is, but alas. NGS has its fans exactly because it's a dumbed down game with a sizable, bland open world, and we all know how well those do even though everyone has something negative to say about them. You should absolutely not play this game unless under *very* specific circumstances and expectations. Those circumstances and expectations are what has made me stick around for 200 some hours, and unless you can fulfill every one of them, I don't think you should play. You probably shouldn't play it anyway.
Anyway.
What circumstances and expectations? 

1. I have a veteran, ride-or-die PSO2 friend that's shown me the ropes and knows how to navigate the byzantine menus and systems. This game is built ontop of the carcass of a game from 2012, and the creaking weight of legacy tech stinks up the room like a corpse. Progression systems are spread across 10 different menus and operates on impenetrable logic unless (unless!) you have a friend who was there from the start to help you navigate the bloat. With that said, the UX is still unpleasant to interact with, with unclear navigation and fumbly controls. 
2. I like fashion and photography and character art. Point-blank, do you? If not, turn elsewhere. PSO2NG has a remarkably robust character creator that allows a level of player expression only really rivaled by Second Life. This means the vast majority of the player-base are some variant of a blow-up sex doll, which has taken some sort of mental toll on me, but it's  sometimes charming in its own depraved sort of way; you can see some truly wild stuff in here. This extends to the housing system, which is equally free-form and Wild West feeling. All in all, in terms of player expression in a multiplayer setting, I haven't really encountered anything better that doesn't require skills in Blender. The tools, awful as they are, are all in-game. 
3. I have never played PSO2 base game. A lot of reviews seem to lament the state of NG, especially in comparison to the old version of the game. I carry no such baggage, and I'm glad I don't. I dislike this game enough as it is! 

With all three points in mind, I've played 200 hours because I do actually enjoy dressing up in cute outfits and doing photoshoots. It's an awful shame then that they insist to attach a "game" to the dolly-dress-up. Let's see...

The combat is boring and monotonous, which they try to hide with a pachinko parlor's worth of noise and colour; the gearing is nonsensical and largely RNG-dependant, filled with baroque systems the game never explains clearly; the open-world is a chore to navigate, needlessly large to make your daily chores take longer; the story is deeply unengaging and I found myself actively hostile to it, skipping every cutscene to just get it over with; the economy is in the gutter with the real money cost for gacha pulls being through-the-roof high, resulting in a player economy that's equally stingy (built by whales, for other whales); the server infrastructure is in an inexcusable state, where if you get disconnected for even more than a few more seconds you get kicked out of your raid, with no possibility to reconnect to it, meaning no reward! From Legacy to Letdown – New Genesis Fails to Uphold the Phantasy Star Name

As someone who’s spent countless hours in Phantasy Star Online (Dreamcast, GameCube) and Phantasy Star Universe, it’s painful to say that New Genesis feels like a massive step backwards — not just from PSO2, but from the series as a whole. This was meant to be a bold new chapter, but what we got was a shallow reimagining that lost much of what made the originals special.

Let’s start with the world. While NGS boasts a large, open-world format, it feels hollow and lifeless. Exploration quickly becomes tedious due to a lack of meaningful content. Gone are the distinct, varied environments of PSO1 or the social hubs and stylish cities of PSU — replaced with bland landscapes and a repetitive cycle of gathering materials and doing the same few tasks.

Combat is faster and flashier, but ironically, it’s also less rewarding. PSO1’s deliberate pacing and meaningful enemy encounters have been traded for mobs that feel like filler. There’s little sense of progression — most classes feel the same by mid-game, and the “build depth” of previous titles is largely absent.

One of the most glaring issues is lack of content and identity. At launch and even well beyond, NGS feels like an early-access shell. The story is wafer-thin, the characters are forgettable, and core features like compelling loot, challenging dungeons, and team-oriented gameplay (a staple of the series) are either undercooked or missing entirely.

The social aspects are a shadow of what they once were. PSO1 and PSU had vibrant lobbies, strong community interaction, and reasons to play with friends. In NGS, despite being an MMO, it often feels like a solo experience with people just running past each other in the open world.

And perhaps most disappointing is the sense that New Genesis tries to be like other MMOs — but loses the unique sci-fi charm, music, atmosphere, and quirky depth that gave the older games their soul. The sleek UIs, gritty space-fantasy tone, and mysterious worldbuilding of the early titles have been traded for generic anime tropes and gacha-driven progression.

Final Thoughts:
Phantasy Star Online: New Genesis is a textbook case of how not to modernize a beloved franchise. Flashier doesn’t mean better, and open-world doesn’t mean deeper. For longtime fans, it’s a heartbreaking regression — a game that feels disconnected from the magic of its predecessors. PSO1 and PSU still stand tall in comparison, despite their age. Sadly, NGS feels like a beautiful but empty shell.

It appears that this is an unfortunate ongoing trend within the gaming industry.

Was gonna keep this short but as i typed it became a bit longer but yeah. I Love Phantasy Star Online. Ive been playing it since i was 8 back on the gamecube. Didnt play much PSO2 cause it took so long to get to come West, but i tried it for a bit and liked it. 

When playing through this games content, the combat feels great (some of the most satisfying, more character-action driven combat than most MMOs in my opinion), exploration is nice, although traversal could use a few more tools i think, and the world spaces look great. 

The issue is there so little of all of it. After 2 years, theres barely 20-30 hours of content to do if you follow the main story AND do all the side content. On top of the fact that most of that side content is THINLY veiled fetch quests and "kill x amount of _" quests, The world spaces that i think look so good, are small as hell, and take less than a few minutes to run across, and what story is there, even when the writing is good, feels low production value. 

Then you get to the "Phantasy Star Online: New Genesis - Ultra Evolution Ver.2 Update" as they LITERALLY CALLED IT THEMSELVES, and its basically just an expanded version of player homes from Base PSO2, with some slight gameplay changes and QOL to the rest of the game. 

After watching their latest "NGS Headline" showing it off, i immediatley came here to uninstall the game and write this review, because until they add some actual, substantial, gameplay, and in-game-world changing/story content, that can keep me engaged for more than 2 hours every 6 months, im done with this game. 

Last thing ill do is leave you with the comment i left on the "Ver.2" Update stream from today on Sega's PSO2:NGS Youtube page. Obviously less measured than my review here, but also my true unfiltered reaction to the "news":

"Jesus Christ, our expectations were already low and yet they still find a way to disappoint us. This is nothing. This is Version 1.0.0.0.2. Like, no hate to the devs, but this game needs new leadership and more resources, because this slow drip of content is a fucking embarrassment.  The vision for this game is so much grander than ANYTHING they've been able to achieve. The "Open World" can be traversed from side to side in less than 10 minutes, the islands/biomes are treated as different continents yet feel barely bigger than most mid-size cities (and less than a few hundred feet apart.) The cutscenes are stiff and mostly uninteresting to watch, even when the story is actually at its best, as well as little things like the fact that in those cutscenes, your character uses the GreatSword weapon, no matter what class you actually are (very nit-picky i know but its immersion breaking in a way i cant recall happening in other MMOs ive played.) And, although a lot of the stuff at the end of Chapter 5 i actually really enjoyed story wise, especially the boss, the world space of Lecielle was linear and uninteresting, and the majority of Chapter 5 leading up to it was literally just fast traveling between regions fighting larger and larger waves of DOLLS, the things weve already fought thousands of. Barely 2 hrs of content and thats partially cause its the one story boss that actually gave me a challenge and i had to try twice.

You would think that most teams, especially for MMOs, would have learned not overpromise and underdeliver, but you would also think that i would have learned not to expect too much from this game when we've barely gotten more than 30 hrs of actual content, which is absurd for an MMO, ESPECIALLY 2 years into its life cycle. 

So i guess thats on me..."

Original review and indepth about UI, keybinds and camera:
The UI, camera and control schemes are a crime against videogames.
Control scheme is meh, but with the biggest offender being the most obtuse re-bindable settings. ALT is forced to be an "emote wheel", and you have no way of changing it. CTRL also cannot be rebinded. Hotbar buttons are also not rebindable and stuck on being numbers 1 til 9, meaning anything beyond 5 is hard to reach and never used without being extremely awkward during battles. 
The UI has ZERO customization, except of "make it bigger". And I don't mean "make this element bigger, this one smaller", no, just make everything big, or make everything small. No change in opacity, no change in location, no change in what is even active and what not on screen, no change in what is where.
Plenty of games do this, but extremely rare to have MMO's not allowing this. And you know, it wouldn't be too bad, if only the UI elements were designed with user experience in mind. Instead, you get popups, tutorials, character dialogues, everything and anything, taking the center of the screen, where all the action is happening, mid fight, and because this game also has a 1990 camera controls of course the UI will be covering 90% of the enemy. Unless you use the free camera, in which case you will miss 90% of the attacks. Unless you use the "camera on shoulder", which look like a 2006 game where 1/3 of the screen is the character, the FOV is awful, and you have no idea of what is going on to your left, to your right, to your feet, to your back, no, you can only see the front.

And all of these awful choices would have been a super minor problem if ONLY they had customization for UI, controls, and a proper camera.
They are so bad, that the aggressive monetization and gachas and the 20 lotteries you are spammed with the moment you finish the prologue before being able to breathe once and the ADS you see during loading screens, are NOTHING compared to the issues with controls camera and UI.

[h2]8 years of waiting completely wasted[/h2]
First started playing PSO2 about 3 years ago, haven't played it in about 2 or so.

I greatly enjoyed what little of PSO that I was able to play back in the Dreamcast days, so when I heard about a sequel being released in 2012 I was on the edge of my seat. Back then though I couldn't read Japanese and there wasn't an official English version so I was a bit screwed. A few years later an unofficial translation patch came out, but me being the sceptical idiot I was, I didn't take advantage of it and opted to simply wait in the hopes of an English official version. Lo and behold, 8 years later we actually got an English release! ...And it was a complete disappointment.
[list]
[*]The biggest and most glaring issue, the size of the damn thing. I just figured 'wow there must be so much stuff to see and do', but no. The bloated file size is due to downloading 2 copies of the game - the original JP game files, and the global release files on top. Why this is a thing is something I never found a good explanation for.

[*]Related to the above point, the actual global server team themselves, and I don't normally go after developers when being critical of a game. Poor support, lack of communication towards players regarding any issues that cropped up, questionable translation quality, they just didn't seem to care.

[*]Content straight up being missing from the original JP version of the game. Case in point - a group of people discovered clothing sets in the game files that hadn't been taken out, they were just unavailable on the global client for some undisclosed reason. Somehow these fellows managed to distribute the clothing sets to themselves and a number of other players. Global team response? Ban everyone involved - including those who had gotten the outfits through trade/market purchase thinking they were legitimate - without appeal and do everything they can to keep the incident quiet. The end.

[*]Shoehorned PvP. I'm entirely willing to admit I'm not a fan of PvP in any MMO, but from what little I saw and what I found out through talking to those who did partake of it is that it was clearly an afterthought. If the bugged mechanics didn't do you in, the zero-stability server would.

[*]'Battle pass' system. This should have been the first and only red flag I needed to switch the game off the moment I started playing, but no. For some reason I decided to keep on in the hopes that it was just a temporary thing. Turns out it wasn't and the entire reason for having it was to simply distribute items that would have been otherwise gained through the multitude of repeating events that take place on the JP server. Apparently the global team decided that'd be too much for us and opted to give us a half-baked fortnite experience instead. Yay.
[/list]

With all the issues listed above and more, you'd think a serious overhaul would be in the works. But no, the final nail in the coffin was whatever the hell the new genesis thing was supposed to be. I'll be entirely honest here, I don't know what it is outside of being a separate gamemode compared to baseline PSO2. I haven't tried it because the day it officially launched was the day I quit playing.

I can't in good conscience recommend this to anyone who wants to play Phantasy Star Online 2. Do what I should have done all those years ago and just download the JP client then throw the translation patch onto it. Don't support whatever this is supposed to be, because ultimately it's an abomination pretending to be something it isn't.

Where do we begin with this? PSO2 (aka New Genesis) is an online ARPG (not MMO as some may be misled to believe) that follows the trials and tribulations of the ARKS military squadron --a special group that harness supernatural abilities known as photons that provide them supernatural strength and finesse-- that defends humanity from the Dark Falz threat. Dark Falz being an entity that transcended from dark matter into a physical form. The protagonist (who is named Ash by default but is never referenced as such) is dragged into an occurrence that swings destiny into another direction when he meets a young woman named Matoi, whom of which requests to be killed. I won't be speaking of the story itself to avoid spoilers, but needless to say it starts off very slow. Anime filler slow. You're basically tasked on running through preset areas cleaning up threats, and occasionally fighting bosses (that get recycled as you go along) while also getting story beats that unveil more of the solar system you're fighting for.

PSO2 has a class system that utilizes different skilsets and weapons. Hunter is your mainstream melee class, Ranger focuses on long range, and Force is a go-between that focuses on techs (or basically magic). There's also Summoner which is one of the most interesting classes with its pet system, but also requires a lot of learning and commitment to get the most out of it. Not a beginner friendly class but one I would suggest trying.

PSO2 is a great game that unfortunately got put on life support to make way for NGS.
NGS is a bad expansion that really needed another year, at least, to make it seem like it's a solid contender to keep the franchise on par with other online RPGs. The story is so dreadfully weak in contrast to PSO2. There are hundreds of mangaka that write compelling stories which put whatever NGS has done to shame. SEGA really dropped the ball hard when they also removed planet based seed exploration for an open world that is mostly empty space and large cliffsides. 

NGS introduced FOMO to appease shareholders, as SEGA had to devise a setup that would keep the population numbers at a "fine" incline. The community has dried up tenfold and it's quite disappointing that only those with Stockholm syndrome are sticking around. I'd say that I'm part of the issue, yet I'm also self aware enough to know that I despise this gameplay design. If you're seeing people idle in the city hubs, then that alone is proof that the game has no merit or worth. It has now turned into a glorified social hub.

Speaking of which, NGS has a high level of degenerates (far more than I ever saw in PSO2) that try to make their characters look as inhumanly erotic as they can go. SEGA are at fault for making clothing that is quite clearly crossing the line, but the players who partake in that are setting a very bad example. There's also open communication in these hubs where groups would get together and either have childish arguments over in-game meta, spam R18 illustrations (known as symbol arts), and engage in erotic roleplay. Thankfully, you can disable such unsightly behavior by blacklisting such players. This has no impact on matchmaking with them.

My play time on Steam isn't reflective of the 5000 hours I have through Xbox One (where I started with the closed beta). Seeing a game that I had so much passion for decline into a deteriorated mess leaves me wondering what happened.

The main way this game keeps a hold of its player-base is fashion, like most online games. You can customise your character to a crazy deep level and there's a massive variety of clothes and gear to obtain. A lot of the end-game and events are oriented around getting new clothing items or emotes. The issue is that the grind to get these outfits is HEAVY. As a free-to-play player, the main way to get the currencies to unlock said outfits is by completing daily and weekly quests which require you to log in for about 1.5 hours everyday. I don't like the idea of games incentivizing logging in everyday. On days that I didn't log in, I felt like I was missing out on something. I avoided starting new games because that would mean that I can't log in on this game.

Speaking to some long term members of the community, I learned that a substantial number of them either do whale or have whaled on this game before. Of course it's possible to be a free-to-play player and still gain the same things that pay-to-win players get, but the paying players will get the newest items a lot faster and the free players will be left with a feeling of FOMO and a massive grind to get these items. At it's core this game is trying to frustrate you into spending your money. People said things akin to "Good luck, enjoy the game, but try not to spend money on it". That's never a good sign.

The 98 hours (at the time of writing) is mostly from the original PSO2. I loved the OG PSO2. NGS... not so much. NGS to me feels like a grindfest. Granted, PSO2 can be that too when grinding for high levels, but in NGS's case, you're grinding levels to be able to progress to the next story mission. As fun and flashy as the combat can be (Katana Braver (and maybe Slayer) go brr), it doesn't make up for how boring things can be. Go to a combat area, grind for 20+ mins to get higher levels, spend meseta for better gear til you get to the required battle level for the next mission, rinse and repeat.

The open world is just meh. NGS is a pretty looking game (when playing on a good enough system), but the world isn't all that interesting. I'm not an open-world kinda person in the first place, so I'm certainly biased in that regard, but running from A to B, occasionally breaking boxes and killing more enemies to complete an event or grind. It's just kinda boring. Not a fan of skill points being locked behind Cocoons and Towers. It gives an excuse to explore the world to look for them and get stronger, but I just don't care for it.

The biggest problem I have with NGS by far is Sega's decision to make the installation of it mandatory if you just want to play base PSO2. And NGS is roughly 60GB, 103GB if you want base PSO2 on top of that. Needing to install NGS, something people may not care for whatsoever, just to play base PSO2 is dumb and just puts a bad taste in my mouth.

I've only gotten to Retem (the second region), and I have little to no desire to progress further. If I boot up the game again, it'll be for base PSO2, not something that feels tiring and boring to go through (albeit something that may be more fun with friends or just people to play with in general if you've got them).

Edit: I did go back to playing NGS coz of the EXP event for combat sectors. I misremembered what point I got up to, I was still in Aelio. I managed to get well past the latest region at the time of writing (Stia) and I assume I still have a surprising amount of story missions to go through. 

Something I noticed was the stupid amount of EXP I got after completing story missions and some tasks. I  never had to grind because I always the required BP to progress the story. The one time I didn't reach a requirement, I just looked around and got better gear, before finding out already had better gear in my inventory.

And that's another thing of note. I'm guessing Sega wants people to get to the latest content coz you get handed free gear that's probably better than most of the stuff you'd get from playing the game organically. I couldn't tell you exactly when they give you the stuff, as most of it seemingly just showed up or I got it as a result of reaching a certain level w/my main class. I'm not exactly complaining, but it's worth pointing out.

Last thing I'll mention is the story. I don't pay much attention to it as I play PSO2 for the gameplay, but it does get seemingly interesting. I can't comment much on it since I just skip cutscenes, but I at least have a slight interest in whatever's going on.

All in all, ig NGS is alright. I still like base more, but NGS, I've found to be 'fine' after coming back. Not great, but not a complete borefest either.

Edit 2: Felt like this for a while now, but NGS has unfortunately felt boring to me again. Sadly, but not particularly surprisingly, most of the things from the old review are still true. I talk about the new stuff here, check the old review towards the end to see more about the game in general.

I can write an essay on this, but I'll keep it brief. 
The two best and most outstanding qualities of this game are its combat and its fashion/character customization. Everything else..and I mean literally everything else about the game is severely lacking and objectively bad, so much so that its frustrating because the aforementioned is really, really good. 
The dev team is very rigid and stubborn and are excrustiatingly slow to balance and update things related to gameplay.

The combat and fashion as I said are the only things the game has going, but if you wanna get into either of them and enjoy them fully, it will require a lot of irl spending. The fashion items and fun emotes and stuff are buyable with ingame money, but the amount of that you will make as free to play would require you to do a mundane activity in game for 8+ hours to afford one, maybe two, items you might be interested in.

If you enjoy gearing and min maxing, then I highly recommend staying away from this game. There are certain weapon drops that are on the level of myths. There's a thing called Fixa which every weapon can have attached to it and it comes in 5 levels and different effect types. They only [b]recently[/b] made it so that the player can recreate this on a weapon that doesn't have it, either by spending a copious amount of free to play resources you accumlate over the course of several months..(for just a rng chance of getting it on one single weapon in the end) or by whaling on the game obscenely hard. Fixa has existed since the game's release and has always been a major point of contention, which took the devs 3 years to even begin to address.

The only way I could recommend this game is if you intend to play it casually on and off. It's arguably perfect for that and can easily be picked up and dropped. The combat is fun and you'll likely find a weapon and class you enjoy playing. All classes function as dps, so if you enjoy playing support in games you might not be as interested. Raids, bosses and whatever else have no real mmo mechanics that require any team oriented strategy..most of the game's strategy is found in optimizing your dps. 

That's about it..and yes, this was brief for how much could be said about the dev team dropping the ball so hard on a game with this much potential. They will never understand the extent to which they harmed and lost the community and following they had going with this franchise. 
Thanks for taking the time to read my review.

I "wasted" 4.7k hours in this game, hoping since launch (back in june 2021) that the game would improve as the foundation was really hitting that itch for me, but it's time to give up. After multiple world expansions (up to 3 new regions, 1 new randomized dungeon and a city exploration with timelimit), multiple class reworks, expansions and updates, after many "new enemies" to fight, player housing, a card minigame and after some new quest types, the game still isn't in an acceptable state. I played the game for this long mostly because of my alliance (guild) in the game and I had fun playing with them, even if the game itself wasn't good.

➤➤ Long Review:

- Story: The story of Base PSO2 is good, but it's majority cutscenes with some fights here and there. The story of NGS however, it's not great. It's slow, boring and somewhat predictable. It did however get somewhat decent with the latest story update, but it wasn't enough for me to say they redeemed the story.

- Gameplay: NGS gameplay originally was one of the stronger parts, but the longer you play it, the more you notice how empty it really is. It looks flashy, but there is no depth. The devs even realized this and added more customization to the attacks, trying the bare minimum to increase the build variety in the game, but for me, this is just a bandaid fix for deeper issues.. Another massive flaw was the overreliance on Dodge/Weapon Actions (A parry/counter unique for each weapon). The devs again realized this and added new mechanics to bosses such as Attacks that can't be avoided with dodge/weapon action, again, bandaid fix for deeper issues. Let's talk about the elements next. Usually, you would think Fire does something different than water or light, but in NGS, they all do the exact same. If the enemy has an elemental weakness, after hitting the enemy often times with that specific element, the enemy will go into "elemental down". That's it. There is no "fire deals damage over time" or "water decreases armor/damage resistance". Besides the "elemental down", there is also the "physical down", which is also the same as the elemental down, but it relies on physical attacks instead of elemental attacks. Now with all of the different classes available and lots of different weapons types, you could just play a different class/weapon combo to fight the boredom, but as mentioned above, the game heavily relies on Dodge/Weapon Action. Every fight with all melee weapons will be the same, the same goes for all ranged weapons and all tech (elemental) weapons. There are some minor differences for each weapons playstyle, but  these are really small. The gameplay also doesn't have the typical 3 roles system for the classes. Yes, you have classes that can "heal" or "buff/debuff", but they're extremely simple, Only 2 Skills that heal, either the same amount as a healing item or Full Life and Full PP (Mana) once with a massive cooldown and 1 buff skill. The Debuff isn't even a skill, instead it's a passive for one specific class which applies when you hit the enemy. Not to mention, all of the skills mentioned above aren't even necessary to clear any content. (Instead of them, the class called "Ranger" is necessary, as this class can apply an effect on an enemy that increases the damage of all people hitting the marked spot, basically making them necessary to have if you want to clear high end content when they launch.)

- Sound: The Soundtrack is actually decent and somewhat memorable. Doesn't feel out of place as well, but as with any soundtrack, you might start to hate them.

- Visuals: The game looks visually decent enough. The world looks nice and the effects are good, but the characters are bad. I don't understand how they thought this style for characters was in any way good. As an active player, you get used to the graphics, but for majority of new players, 90% of characters just look straight up awful and in some cases, it's not even the player's fault. They tried to "fix" this by adding a cel shading option to the game for all characters or just yours. This however isn't enough in my opinion. The foundation is already flawed and shows cracks. Just watch the reveal for the Atelier Ryza collab with NGS. The NGS versions of Ryza and co. look awful.

- Collabs: Yes, the game has collabs, quite a lot actually. From Eminence in shadow and Frieren to Atelier Ryza and Melty Blood, tons of collabs here, HOWEVER. The collabs are really barebones. In the beginning, all you got was "AC Scratch Tickets", (Real Money Gacha) for the cosmetics of the collab IPs. That's it. Now, You also get cardboard cutouts of these characters to place in your Creative Space (Player Housing), AMAZING! No quests, enemies, stories, nothing. The only exception being the Sonic "Collabs" if you want to call them that. Instead of "AC Scratch Tickets" with the cosmetics, we got Limited Time Quests somewhat Sonic themed. They were ok the first time, but they get boring really really fast.

- The only positive of NGS that no other MMO currently tops: Character Customization. The character creator in NGS is surprisingly deep and good. You have tons of sliders that actually change the character. You have the ability to mix and match outfit parts (which are separated into 3 layers, Outerwear, Base/Setwear and innerwear). You also can freely customize your whole character and change everything about it with no barriers. Want to change the Gender? Do it. Don't want to be a human anymore, change to a CAST (Robot). Now with all the years of NGS behind us, there are tons and tons of different outfits, hairstyles, accessories, motions and so on that you can use to create truly unique characters ... IF you either scratch (pay for the gacha) or grind yourself to death for the ingame money.

- I skipped so many other flaws and problems. There is no Trading between Players, the player market Search is horrendous, gear progression is boring, content gets repeated (especially normal enemies), the community is extremely horny and down bad, Rewards for "difficult" content is really demotivating, the game is p2w, the game punishes you if you play for free, The tutorials are bad (if there are even any tutorials explaining specific things), the open world isn't being used at all, majority of content gets obsolete in few months, and and and ...

PSO2 is an iconic game, and one of the most successful anime action RPGs of all time, I want to call it an MMO but it really isn't - story content is solo and most of the multiplayer content can be done solo also. A few endgame urgent quests will be near impossible to do alone, and at this point of the game, you probably will never do them anyway as PSO2 is practically neglected to death in favor of their PSO "2.5" New Genesis.
New Genesis brings a lot of new things to the table: Improved graphics, a semi open world, better character customization, and more modern gameplay (that means casualized, but stylized and more responsive)
However, it has crushed the expectations of most of the original PSO2 fans almost entirely and I will explain why:
New Genesis has completely fumbled the legacy it was given from PSO2. As the name "New Genesis" suggests, the developers decided it would be a smooth move to ride the fame of PSO2 with a game that practically has nothing to do with it anymore - your player character might be the same character as the one in PSO2, but they haven't confirmed anything yet, and I won't go spoiling anything here.
Another thing they botched was was the combat customization and skilltrees, but I will admit that they have done some leaps towards a better direction over the years of it's lifetime.
That said, the core gameplay itself has barely evolved at all since launch, as you are still mostly just playing rhythm games with enemies, spamming and abusing invulnerability from parry/counterattacks.
Anyway, I'm not too good at deconstructing it, so I'll get simple.

The good:
+ One of the best character customization options in MMORPG genre (though this does not apply to the character creator much, and I still don't want to call it an MMO)
+ Smooth gameplay (Dumbed down, far easier than PSO2, but it's still a lot more responsive and free)
+ A pretty open world (though it's sparsely used for anything after initial exploration)
+ A great home building system "creative space", one of the best I've seen in an MMO

The bad:
- Neglected PSO2 to the point where it's all but dead
- NGS combat is not very customizable and most classes play too similarly to each other, lacking proper identity (the skill trees will give you almost everything, making a unique playstyle is nearly impossible - even after they added things like "MARS" and a couple of skill variations, the latter in particular is extremely unnoticeable compared to PSO2 where skill customization could make the ability and class function almost entirely differently)
- Bad story (they tried to fix it later, though I haven't gone back to see if anything's improved)
- Boring endgame and the leveling process is fast (After you've done all the story content, and whatever good urgent quests there are, you'll be left doing nothing but pointless grind and the drop rates are horrible)
- EXTREMELY UNFRIENDLY TOWARDS F2P PLAYERS (You cannot even sell things without premium membership subscription or rare 3 day shop passes)
- ingame trading was removed in NGS (They probably did it solely to fish more microtransaction purchases)
- Ingame marketplace is completely crap (The prices are insane, the item search is too specific and a lot of toxic players are playing stock market and monopoly with it, making buying cosmetics or earning money very hard unless you're a whale who basically trades real money in to In-Game money)
- a cesspool of degenerate players (but you're free to decide if that's a flaw or not yourself)
- almost unused openworld (it isn't very rewarding to do anything outside of urgent quests or dailies)

It IS a fun game, but the fun is drained rapidly - there is hardly any reason to dump hundreds of hours in to this game, which most people are doing anyway.
The actual endgame content isn't the gameplay at all, is pretty much just customizing your character(s), what I mean is that everyone is just standing in the lobby "cities" flexing their latest whale cosmetics such as expensive and distasteful bikinis.
A lot of people tend to make freaky unnatural anatomies on their characters, among other monstrous creations. (Some people have a good sense of humor or some great looks, but the majority doesn't :D)

IF you want to play this game, I very much discourage it - it is designed to make you want to pay money.
You can play F2P, but it is never ending inventory management and lack of money/storage space.
Now, if you still want to play it despite all of the complaints, feel free, but I strongly advise you not to support SEGA on this one, and don't get attached, they will either pull the plug suddenly, or take YEARS before the game is in a state where people want to actually come back to it, so it's not worth investing in to. If I was a new player, I'd just play the story and leave it at that..

This is my in-depth review directed towards the "New Genesis" Game, not the legacy game hidden behind it. Steam state's that I played this game 4,6k+ hours, but in actuality I've clocked in double, heck even triple the amount of time since I played during the Microsoft launch BETA.

Game doesn't respect your time. Not much else to say, let's move on.

- [Combat rewards are extremely unrewarding.] This one is a HUGE one for me. There is nothing more debilitating than watching last or current season's gear fall right into your inventory, only for it to be scrapped into a measily 80 meseta or however much it's worth. The only way for gear bit's to be worth any shread of Meseta, would be via Fixa's, but at that point you're just asking yourself if you want to slave away for copium drops. You can spend hours, days, weeks, even MONTHS, before you can even see something viable to even sell in the shop. When I got the Sega Dreamcast in 2000, Phantasy Star Online was the first role-playing game I played on that console. I spent countless hours battling alongside friends, taking on bosses, and trading weapons and items just for fun.

Now, twenty years later, Sega has released the sequel: Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis. Due to licensing issues, it took nearly a decade to reach the North American market. While I was excited to see another entry in the series, New Genesis has been a disappointing experience. The game bears little resemblance to its predecessors; it’s more open-world and feels like a fashion simulator than a true RPG.

The story is set 1,000 years after the events of the original Phantasy Star Online 2, with Ark settling on Planet Halpha. The antagonist Dark Falz returns, but the narrative falls flat. The characters, Aina, Manon, Dozer, and Crawford, are underdeveloped, with minimal backstory or emotional depth. This lack of character development makes the experience frustrating and, at times, dull.

By contrast, the original game sent players on a gripping rescue mission to Planet Ragol to uncover the fate of Rico Tyrell, the principal’s daughter aboard Pioneer Two. New Genesis fails to capture that epic tone, instead pitting players against a new enemy called the Starless. The setting shifts from life aboard a starship to a fortress-based existence, losing much of the original’s charm.

Gameplay now resembles an arcade shooter, offering more freedom of movement. Players can fly, and feeding your Mag, a small machine that generates powerful attacks, is no longer required. On the plus side, new features like Creativespace allow players to build cities, museums, craft objects, and houses. It’s a neat addition, but overall, the game feels more like a sandbox than a structured RPG.

Graphically, New Genesis is a step up from its predecessor, with vibrant colours and expansive environments including mountains, volcanoes, deserts, snowfields, and hidden cities. However, the game lacks the story-driven campaigns that made earlier titles engaging. The open-world design sacrifices the linear level progression that once made gameplay so satisfying.

The soundtrack also falls short, failing to create an immersive atmosphere.

Final Verdict: Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis earns a 6.8 out of 10. It’s visually impressive but lacks the soul and structure that defined the original.

An experiment by SEGA to see if they could dip into the open world theme park style made popular by Zelda:BotW and Genshin Impact. After years in the oven, great examples to build off of (PSU, PSO2), and several years after release, it's just a social platform dress-up simulator milking it's audience for gacha $$$ and the promise of something greater that may never be.
-----------------------------------------------------------
The story and setting do not tap into a fraction of the potential that the Phantasy Star series is capable of. NGS has been out for 3 years now and it's story amounts to an amateur anime arc with filler. On top of that it has been isolated to a tiny boring island the entire time. This is a sci-fi fantasy game with a history of space exploration and universal threats. The characters are likable, but shallow. In most cases a strong contrast to PSO2's character designs.

Before we get into this, I need to note, my review is influenced by an upcoming change, slated for Monday, 11/6/23, at 1 AM EST (or 11/5/23, 10 PM PST).

WOULD I RECOMMEND PSO2/New Genesis TO NEW PLAYERS?  Currently, ABSOLUTELY NOT.  While any game has its ups and downs, and deep down I do love the game / series, there's definitely pros and cons, and the upcoming change is a MAJOR addition to the cons list.

Pros:
- Combat flows very smoothly, and the attacks are very flashy
- The music is truly fantastic, some of the best songs I've heard in a game.
- Character creation is one of the most complex/full-bodied systems I've seen in an MMO -- while the face and body customization aren't quite on the level of BDO or better, the accessory system allows a LOT more freedom for end results.
- Beautiful and unique scenery
- What little bit of story is in NGS is decent.
- Hanging out with friends, like with any MMO, is a good time.
- Creative Spaces, one of the newer features, is a pretty great iteration on base/house building mechanics.

Cons:
- For as smooth as combat is, it gets very samey after a while.  Each weapon just has their optimal 1 or 2 attacks, and that ends up being basically all you use outside of very rare and specific situations.
- Rampant and greedy monetization.  Most content pumped out, over the last 2 and a half years, has been cosmetic gachas.  If you want to be able to sell anything, be it drops from said gachas, or drops you get after hundreds of hours of farming (that'll be the next point), you need to fork over roughly $15 USD per month, or use the single-time pass for 3 days of shop access that you get less than once per month.  Freemium currency is also used a lot, but sources of it in-game dry up very quickly, and sells for an absurdly inflated cash price if you cave (do not cave).
- Drop rates of anything of actual value in the game are ABSURDLY low.  We're talking lower than most MMO's END-GAME LOOT tables.  Quite literally, the last big set of weapons had, at the time, an estimated drop rate of 0.0000002%.  It's not fun or rewarding, it's a lottery.  Fans in both the Global and JP regions have given feedback on this multiple times, which has been acknowledged, but then completely disregarded / doubled-down upon.  This makes the game feel incredibly unrewarding, with most players never seeing BIS weapons before they become irrelevant again.
- Content updates at a snail's pace, and the last half a year has added no new MSQ battles, only a handful short 30-60 second cutscenes.  Basically no interaction in the main-story, in all that time.  First act of the game isn't even completed, we're just on Episode 1, Chapter 6 part 3, and the (actually exciting) plot hook at the end of chapter 5 hasn't gone anywhere yet (that was over 6 months ago).  Current content, outside of story, is just a level increase in older areas.  Which they've already done two previous times in the same maps.
- Mishandling by Sega has left the playerbase in a state of constant atrophy.  We're looking at less than 8k players per day, on average (and only roughly 2k players on steam per day), and that number has been in steady decline since Spring. 
 Thankfully it's cross-platform, but it does still result in the game feeling a bit like a ghost-town.  However, Sega's solution was to delete most blocks, forcing all these players into congested hubs instead, which ALSO negatively impacts game performance for many.  (Also, the game can only render 50 characters, at maximum, at one time, so, on days with very low block counts / higher than average online players, you might not be able to see most of your friends because strangers filled up the render limit when you load in)
- Lots of arbitrary limits -- limited accessory slots, seemingly random "point costs" assigned to them that can't go over another arbitrary point cost limit, limited build gauges in the creative spaces (but they give much larger limits in alliance(this game's version of a guild/free company) spaces, so it's not a hardware issue at all), caps on non-currency points you can earn per day/week, etc.  No reason behind some of them (accessories being the only one with some kind of reasoning, but the point costs still make no actual sense), Sega just likes limiting what you're allowed to do / your creativity.
- MOST IMPORTANTLY, the new change coming on the 5th/6th -- Sega is switching the anti-cheat from GameGuard (which isn't particularly great, to be fair) to the incredibly intrusive Wellbia XIGNCODE3.  While you can "opt out," it will still be downloaded and installed to your PC.  For those not in the know, XC3 has a reputation of running at all times in the background once installed, whether a game is using it or not  It also has been known to scan personal/unrelated files, transmit personal information (making it a potential violation of NDAs or HIPAA laws if you use your PC for both work and play -- also, on their part, their practices violate laws in much of Western Europe and the Americas), increasing CPU performance loads / power usage at all times, being an overall security risk for the consumer, etc.  It installs with kernel level access, too, which is far from great.  On top of that, it's been known to cause MANY false-positive reports, flagging AMD's anti-lag features, VPNs, Linux OSs, third party keyboard/mouse/fan management systems, etc., as attempts at cheating and automatically calling for a permanent ban of the player.  The constant intrusions of privacy, and consistent false-flagging, has led to most games in the western market that used Wellbia to scrap it in under a year and issue a massive apology, compensation, etc. but Sega seems to not know or not care.

First let me clear some things since I'm not sure if I can make 2 reviews. This game is actually 2 games. The first is the base PSO2 game that everyone knows and loves from 2012-2021, and the second is NGS which came out at the start of 2021 and is still ongoing. To keep things simple I will refer to the original game as PSO2, and the new one as NGS. You can hop between PSO2 and NGS relatively quickly by just Transferring the block your on (The elevators in PSO2 and the Ryuker Device in NGS), or you can load into them by selecting them after trying to log onto your character (I think new characters automatically start in NGS.)

          With that out of the way let me start with PSO2. PSO2 is a dungeon crawler with the only MMO aspect being the same as Destiny. You can only see random players in the hub, and 12 of them can be in each instance for one map. The game originally came out in 2012, so the game obviously looks really dated and the gameplay is clunky at best. Also the wiki is going to be a must at some points. Honestly if you play old MMOs a lot, you'll feel right at home. It's a very solid experience despite guides being a must. I can't really say much bad about the gameplay since it's what you would expect out of 2012. You can also get around the clunky movement by using certain arts to make movement more smooth, which does hinder the very early game when you don't have them. In terms of story I really liked it, but I can see it not being for everyone. It's a bit basic and kinda predictable, but still somehow really good with some things you wouldn't expect (not counting the thing from the start of EP4 that was just stupid). The English voice acting is also what you would expect from a niche JP game in 2012. Which is to say... not good. You do eventually get use to it though, and it even has a bit of a charm to it. At least until the summoner chick I always forget the name of becomes a character. Her VA is somehow worse than every other VA by a large margin and every time she speaks, I get pulled out of the experience.

          The monetization for PSO2 isn't necessarily the best, and most certainly is more predatory than what western gamers are use to, but I never felt the need to buy AC (Premium currency) or a membership. Although when EP6 came out the in game economy was destroyed by events that made getting large amounts of Meseta (F2P currency) stupid easy. Now what does this have to do with monetization? Well about a month later with those events finally coming to an end, NGS finally releases, and they take f2p methods of selling items on the shop away. Making it so that only premium players can sell items. Well due to the large amount of inflation in the game premium players are able to make millions of Meseta easily and f2p players are screwed. This means if you're f2p, no cool cosmetics, or buying gear that has stats you want to transfer. You have to farm all that yourself and risk destroying your armor every time you augment it. Even if you have 100% success rate boosters, it will take forever to get everything minmaxed and still be very expensive. For me that's not much of an issue since I enjoy the grind, but I don't think most people would want to go through that. I'm sure there's more, but it's been a few years since I played this game hardcore, so I can't remember everything. I just remember there's more freemium things that got turned into premium exclusives, that made me quit alongside the tiny playerbase (which seems to be more populated as of writing this).

          Finally NGS, the most current title in the Phantasy Star Online IP. It's advertised as an expansion to the base game, but is really an entirely new game that you can hop between with just a little loading screen that everyone is use to anyways. It's an open world MMO that's segmented into instances of lobbies that fit 8 players. You can see the border of each area with a white translucent wall whenever you get close to it. You can make it so you're in a private instance and people will only show up in the hub areas, or just let the game automatically join one. The gameplay feels smooth and responsive as well as the movement. Unfortunately that's where the good ends for the gameplay in NGS. The new enemy types aren't fun to fight against, the world is just big, but doesn't have anything interesting and nothing fills the world. Combat is way to easy and can be boiled down to spamming 1-2 abilities, and Gunner/Ranger is completely broken somehow trivializing combat even more. All the quests are boring and uninteresting which would be the same as the base game, except the base game has fun combat to carry it. Honestly game feels like a chore to play.

          The story so far for NGS... exists. Ep1 finally finished and honestly it's not any better than Ep1 in the base game. Right now it actually feels worse, but that could just be because we're missing context that will get brought up in later episodes so I'm not going to go to deep on this one. Bad starts to stories happen in pretty much every MMO as they always need to start with the world building and then we have to wait for months for the next part. I will say that having to wait 6 months for each major update isn't helping with it either, since the global servers went through 12 years of updates in order within 1 year.

         NGS seems to be split between being known as a stain on PSO2 and an alright game. I'm not sure what the majority think as the player count says the main fan base was split in the middle. Obviously everyone who is like me, and is very disappointed in NGS's release as well as the handling of PSO2 after the fact, is going to be very vocal about it. The player count before NGS was hovering between 4-5k vs rn which seems to be 2k-3k on average. That is still a large portion of players to loose, and I'm not even counting the new players it gained from all the marketing. PSO2:NGS peaked at the launch of the expansion with roughly 60k players, but lost about 22% of them. A portion of that was roughly 50% of their main playerbase from base PSO2.




           TLDR: PSO2:NGS is basically 2 games. The base game from 2012 is great, still probably worth experiencing, but is clunky and a few features were taken out to make people play the other game that flopped off launch and hasn't gotten any better. Is completely finished with no major updates, and it's story concluded. Voice acting is bad, but charming (mainly cause it's from 2012.
          NGS which is an "expansion" but built completely from the ground up in a new engine and plays fundamentally different in every way. It's boring, the story isn't far enough along, updates are 6 months apart, and it's even more predatory than the base game was. At this point, it has fallen off over time and is largely not worth getting into. The biggest thing NGS has going for it is the quality of the character creator, but gacha outfits, especially for T2/Female characters, is nearly the sole focus of development as it would seem. I'd look for another MMO with a more thriving community as well as engaging and re-playable experience and leave this one to the people already stuck here.

Originally, the idea was to play PSO2 and, funny enough, I began my journey exactly when NGS was released.
I may not have as much time as other players, nor am I a seasoned veteran of the PSO2 Classic times... but I've played my fair share of both PSO2 and NGS, leveled half classes in Classic up to max level and all NGS classes to max.

I have seen the growth of this game since June 2020.

[h1]The Good:[/h1]
• PSO2: NGS is a aesthetically pleasing game with beautiful graphics, animations and a fluid and responsive combat system. 
• The place where this game will shine the most, however, is the CHARACTER CREATOR. This is NGS's best attribute by far. I have not seen an anime based game that has a character creator as good as this one. The amount of modifications you can do, paired with clothing, accessories and other animations you'll definetely become the character you want to be... for better or worse...
• The combat system is fluid and each class has a depth to discover depending on the weapons you have and the add-ons you obtain. You'll feel strong running, gliding and attacking enemies! The weapons are varied, most classes having at least 2 weapons you can use (with a few 1 weapon classes). You can mix and match some weapons based on certain parameters (Class and Sub-Class) and you can create your combat style as you see fit with a varied of skills and special attacks.
• Some bosses do offer a good, hard challenge and you feel good when beating them for the first time.
• Another of this game's strongest attributes is the amount of fashion items at your disposal. It is ludicrous how much clothing and accessories you can obtain. When I said you can become the character you want to be...that was not a joke. The sky is the limit. 
• You get plenty of ways to obtain fashion, some are free, others are through in-game challenges, others are through gacha mechanics…but we’ll get to that later on.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]
Yes. We are here already. Quite quickly. Mind you, I do love this game with all my heart, but I cannot deny it has pretty severe flaws.
• A problem with the character creator is that while you can create ALMOST whatever you want...it is limited to some extents and it penalizes you for making thicker characters 
• This game makes dresses and anything that is not touching the skin of a character look puffy on thicker characters. Not all fashion outfits are like that, but most are and it’s an issue that plagues many players.
-The Gameplay-
• While, yes, the gameplay and combat is fluid and fun...the variety is not there. Each class has a total of 4 Photon Arts (special attacks), a guard/counter button and a normal attack button. That's it. While some Photon Arts can become technically 8 (some classes allow to divide 1st half and 2nd half of an attack) it is still not a big variety of abilities you can use. 
• Now, you probably saw that I never mentioned anything about loot and gameplay loop on "The Good" section. That's because there really isn't one. Loot is absolutely atrocious. Sure, you obtain materials to make a very specific set of weapons but other than paltry in-game money, you obtain almost nothing of worth. The worthy items are locked on events or on doing Solo content.
• The gameplay loop of the game is to do dailies, level up, finish story and then...fashion! There is nothing worthy to fight or grind for other than to complete everything.
• Yes, there is solo content, and I am adding it here because this is not something a MASSIVE MULTIPLAYER ONLINE GAME should have plenty of. The good loot, which is about to not be good in a very short time, is locked behind SOLO CONTENT. But wait~! It gets worse!
• As all MMORPG's there is a story to play here. Yes. It's solo content. No. It is NOT GOOD AT ALL. From the 6 chapters released at the making of this review, only the last had something of value and then again it was valuable for PSO2 Classic players, otherwise you won't understand nor feel anything. The characters are bland, boring and underdeveloped, you do not see development at all, it's very hard to care for the story characters at all. You can probably finish all of the story in a week if you played daily…which I do not recommend at all.
• Yes, this gets it’s very own section because while it’s good there is a player shop it is Also ABSOLUTELY BAD. Searching items is a pain in the butt and while buying through it is free, selling on it is not. 
• This game has a “Premium Subscription”. No, it’s not like other games. One would think they pay monthly or annually. Not here. You need to buy AC (the premium currency) or a DLC pack that comes with Premium. Then you need to log into the game and use AC to get a Premium Ticket, or obtain the DLC rewards with the Premium Ticket, and then you need to use the Premium Ticket to be premium. Wow.
• Premium does has some benefits. Some are real QoL, like auto-sell feature for all that loot gear that you do not need, or an additional storage, or additional buffs when you buff yourself up…or the worst of all… THE ABILITY TO SELL ITEMS THROUGH THE PERSONAL SHOP. Worse part of it all is that it’s the only way to give items to other players. There is no Trading on NGS, but there is on PSO2 Classic and yes, you need premium to use it.
[h1]The Ugly[/h1]
• Gacha is probably one of the biggest problems in the game and the only prevalent thing that gets updated every week or month. PSO2: NGS is PLAGUED by the gacha monsters. You do not need it to play, nor to be a decent player, but if you want that “be whoever you want to be” part for your character you cannot escape the gacha, or how we call it in-game: AC Scratches.
• Want cool fashion? AC Scratches. Want cool weapon camos? AC Scratches. Want cool modifier add-ons for your weapons? AC Scratches. Everything is an AC Scratch. The absolute best weapon modifiers you obtain through AC Scratches. That does not means you are locked out of them if you don’t wanna pay, you just gotta buy them in the Personal Shop… at the cost of an arm and a leg.
• The good stuff will always be in the personal shop. Fashion, weapon modifiers, weapon camos, almost all of the cool stuff is on it and you will CRY with how expensive things are on most Ships (Servers). You want that very cool looking hair? That’s 23 million meseta (in-game money). How fast can you get that without paying? Maybe in 24hrs of non-stop farming. More time if you take breaks… BUT BETTER HURRY BECAUSE MAYBE SOMEONE WILL GET IT BEFORE YOU.
• This takes me to the point of FOMO. While the FOMO is not as strong here as in other games, you’ll see it and you’ll feel it. There are collabs in this game with anime, vtubers and other videogames. Those items will come, fly and very probably never come back.
• This is a problem that carried from PSO2 Classic. We are drip fed here. A week worth of Story was drip fed for over 5 years. Content is slow to appear, no class updates (but rebalancing does happen), no story updates, no valuable gameplay updates at all.
• While we are informed of the games upcoming things through a monthly live-stream, the reality of things is that this is the second problem of this game. We do not have content and the content we have gets monotonous extremely quickly, making a lot of people leave. The only thing to really do is fashion, dailies and grind for in-game money. That’s it.

Because while I have a soft spot for PSO2 base game, with the release of NGS, they completely abandoned it, and no newcoming hotfixes that try to pump the dead heart of this game series is going to resuscitate it unless they release an altogether new game - and no, not another attempt at NGS. Goodnight, PSO, May they not desecrate your corpse for long - for it is too late for them to not have done it at all.

However dext farming requires a more specific set up to min/max in which in a good group or a private farm you make 1.5m-2m meseta per hour spent (with either meseta boosters or 100% Rare Drop Boosters + 1 Hour Auto Sell Passes as the drops there adds up to your meseta count when auto-sold.)

Making friends and connections will do you wonders in the game, both Classic and NGS.

Here are several of the critical issues I noticed in this game:
- Multiple currencies used for purchasing items in-game, AC and SG. Classic money-layering obfuscation tactic that should be illegal, with the sad industry standard practice for these things of having items cost just slightly more or less than the denominations of currency that are purchased to try getting you to buy more, and even worse many being basically gambling for a chance at an item.
- Being that this is an RPG it has a sort of talent or skill point system, many MMO players might expect some friction to respec-ing, but will be shocked this game will require you spend real-life money on an in-game currency (500 AC=$5 USD) to buy a secondary talent tree to then utilize for resetting talent trees by spending the other in-game currency (100SG=500ac=$5USD) for a reset pass on the newly purchased "un-set" tree and repeating the second step of this process-and payment-each time you need to reset a class' skill tree. That practice inexcusably abusive, and can only be somewhat overlooked by virtue of how universally shallow the skill trees are currently. SEGA gave out reset passes a few times in the past, but as of the last couple major updates has decided not to, so relying on them would really leave you out to dry if you were to mis-click and accept a bad spec or wanted to change things up when new skills are added in a big update.
- Nearly all the unique fashion/fashion accessories that allow for the much lauded character customization aspect of this game require "scratching" using one of the secondary currencies (AC + SG) for a chance at winning it from a pool of prizes in typical Gacha fashion. Similarly you must also spend money to obtain secondary currency (SG) to make adjustments to your character's physical appearance and the colors of your outfits each time (Color Change Pass, Salon Pass) 
-The market is established in such a way that the actual in-game, in-world currency of Meseta is primarily obtained by selling the fashion items bought with real money on the player market--a market which can only be accessed with purchase of a player shop pass which costs real money. The F2P experience is a 3day pass, once a month, obtained by completing dailies for approximately a week or two. Because doing activities in-game yields only slightly more than not playing the game altogether, your only real chance at obtaining the fashion items is spending real money for AC to then "scratch" aka Gacha RNG slot machine mechanics.
-The game is infected with RNG mechanics that are clearly deliberate as a means of impeding player progress to encourage real-money purchases.  Once you spend the often absurd amount of time to obtain 10x of a rare capsule obtained via RNG drops with extremely low rates, you'll see the max probability of success to affix it will sometimes be as low as 70%. Because of the nature of RNG, even at 95% you can fail multiple times losing the item and any success rate booster items, and aside from that, there's literally nothing to say the game isn't lying about this probability number either as they would have every incentive to do so, to get you "scratching" with real money for a chance at obtaining a 100% chance addi capsule relevant to your class, or maybe purchasing the augment protection by "recycling" the duplicates of items you spent real money on. There are also "add-on skills" in which you are effectively spending Meseta to gamble in hopes of getting a bonus level of what, in any other game including the base PSO2 game, would have been basic class stat bonuses or skill tree options. RNG to get the gear to drop(which you can improve by paying real money for "Rare Drop Rate +x% booster" items), RNG to get the capsules to upgrade the gear, RNG gamble to use the capsules to upgrade the gear, then more RNG gambling to upgrade base stats.
-Inventory is limited, with options for paid expansion. Any items dropped outside of Urgent/Limited/Trainia Quests, basically the majority of the game, will be automatically picked up with no -free- options to stop this from happening. Naturally, the game will drop such a plethora of items that often do not stack, and increase with each event and new region, so as to inconvenience and frustrate you into investing real money into expanding your inventory and storage. Fully upgrading your inventory will cost you about 40 USD. Fully upgrading your "Character Storage"-basically like a bank from WoW- will cost you around 120 USD. You can also rent storage blocks out for various time allotments, 30-90 days for 5 to 12 dollars, respectively. There's a lot of complexity to the storage situation but ultimately none of it would be necessary if not for the poor handling of item drops and forced pickup, which is clearly intentional. There's also a paid auto-sell feature, but it has been rendered useless twice (removal of most drops in Kvaris, then Introduction of Gold/Silver PSEf burst inv flood) and ultimately you're still going to need more storage for holding the various items you'll want/need or you will need to more regularly stop during combat to clear space to prevent potentially losing items.
-Almost every update consists of more gacha fashion items to gamble real money away for than any sort of meaningful content to play within the game, which is something the game desperately and glaringly needs. Watch any of the official PSO update videos they release to see this on full display. 
-There are clearly traps intended to have you spend money for poor/non-existent value items and services in the game. Every death you're offered the chance to buy a scape doll to revive for 100AC/$1USD, Rare Drop rate boosters starting from 800AC/$8USD which you have no way of knowing is actually doing anything-a placebo-since purported rate boost while seemingly large (+100%) is multiplicative against an infinitely minute number, although it's also believed by many to not directly improve the drop rate of rares specifically, and instead the rate chance of drops altogether which would to some degree as well increase the chance of a rare dropping--ultimately extremely convoluted and dishonest system of dubious benefit which expires even when you're doing nothing or logged out. Like a casino selling you a lucky rabbit's foot at the entrance for a few hours.
I'm sure I've missed some things, but I felt it was important that this was highlighted in a review for any would-be player. This is the product of companies hiring pyschologists onto dev teams and papers being published on how to manipulate vulnerable people into spending money. It has been woven into the fabric of this game, which by its lineage should simply have been a 3D verson of a Diablo clone in a sci-fi world inherited from the old Phantasy Star games like the original on Dreamcast. Apart from the critical issues I noted, the game has many glaring gameplay/user experience flaws all of which are probably due at least in part to this focus on monetization above all else. The idea of establishing a fun gameplay loop, with a rewarding payout for time invested as is typical of RPGs with character progression, is almost non-existent. Nothing as yet worth even trying to build a character up for, since the end-game can only be doing what you did to originally build the character up: best analogy would be like leveling up in WoW only to grind mobs in the open world and do dailies-no raids, no dungeons, no interesting loot or gear that comes from any specific place/boss or lore tying any of anything in the barren world together. Every kill just a pull on the slot machine, there aren't any unique named npcs or enemies anywhere in the open world and rare enemies are merely silver/gold colored normal enemies. Items you get are literally just stats, no flavor text, no descriptions whatsoever, no importance or value given to them. Complete degeneration, degredation of the PSO/Phantasy Star brand. Truly saddening.

There's... a LOT to say about New Genesis. I've played for 2200+ hours at this point, and while I do think there's a lot of good points in favor of this game, there's also, like, a ton of bad points.

But those 2200+ hours were also not spent entirely in NGS. So take my rating with a grain of salt, because I'm gonna review base game and NGS like they're separate games.

Let's start with base PSO2. For a game that's been in development hell for 10+ years on the global side, hearing exactly why made things... interesting. But in the 2 years I spent in base game, it was a good time! There was a huge level of customization, the content was coming out at a rather quick pace(A point I WILL brush on later), and bosses and characters that were actually fun to meet and learn about. Getting to know base game in such a short amount of time was actually somewhat daunting, but rewarding for those who wanted in for the lore. The Dark Falz in this game were all interesting concepts, including the done-again concept of fighting yourself, and how the people around the Dark Falz individuals' hosts acted when it came to those hosts was actually interesting, because it isn't like the JRPG trope of fighting a big, bad manifestation of evil and darkness that plans to destroy everything. The Falspawn, and Dark Falz by extention, prey on actual character flaws that lead to them falling to the darkness, and I loved it. Getting to fight and even redeem every single one of them by Episode 6 was super fun.

Of course, if I'm talking base game, I have to talk Episode 5. In the JP side of base game, Episode 5 was probably the worst time to be a PSO2 player. A huge deviation from Episode 4, which in itself was a deviation from Episodes 1-3, was not what the playerbase needed at the time it came out. For hardcore Phantasy Star fans, there are some fun themes in here, notably the return of Alis as a main character, but that whole story was a mess, for something that was supposed to touch upon the origins of the Photoners. There's a lot of interesting ideas in there, but not every bit of it was executed well enough. However, Episode 5 still has some great boss fights, including Masquerader, a clear highlight to the point that my old Alliance and I would run it despite Episode 6 being the endgame.

Overall, with the absolute mountain of content delivered over the course of 2 years, super fun classes and a great combat system that admittedly could be more fluid, PSO2 is an absolute blast, and if you REALLY want to get to know PSO2, I highly recommend starting here before NGS.
