I have to admit right now that NGS is way better now than it was at the start. At launch, there was practically no content, apart from Gigantix, and one episode. Just one. Now we have 7 episodes, and we're actually about to be stronger than we ever were in base game. It's gonna be interesting. But not in a good or bad way.

I want to begin here by talking about the positives I see in NGS. I love the fluidity of combat here. It's probably one of the best playing action combat systems I've played in any MMO. SEGA obviously knows how to make a great combat system in any game, but it shows here. Furthermore, I actually really like the open worlds. 4 different environments to explore with wildly changing landscapes depending on where you look, different biomes inside those 4 environments, and even the Nameless City all look great. Absolute eye candy as far as the eye can see. And lastly, I have to give praise to the improvements to the character creation system. Allowing absolute freedom in character creation means you can make literally ANYONE you want to play as. Cosplays and OCs all look absolutely fantastic, and are worth the time you put into it. Phashion, as they say, is the real endgame here.

That's the problem.

There's barely any endgame content outside of the Duel Quests, and even then, only Masquerader, the one returning endgame boss that you can take on again and again, is the only one that's actually worth it. And while we're not at the rarity of 15*, it's super noticable that the power level curve looks like a hill when you look at a player spread. While you DO have to put time into the meta, the meta's just something you do if you prefer having absolute power. 

The combat system is also limited. Less photon arts means less creative combos, and I'm getting really tired of using the same 4 moves outside of active skills, which are few and far between. Every class is guilty of this, too, and combos can become so stale after a while. 

The Gigantix are boring due to the fact that there's no unique mobs that can ONLY be Gigantix. When you fight them, they're just like the regular bosses/mobs, meaning the real challenge is just in pattern memorization. 

The story was boring, too. In a game where you're supposed to be the main character, it feels more like you're just the hard carry side character, and that's all you exist to do. It took about 5 chapters for our characters' past to become relevant, and that's if you played base game. 

It's supposed to be that our character is supposedly the actual Guardian from base game. We were somehow sent 1000 years into the future, with no objective, goal, or even our memories, starting from scratch and growing back into the warriors we used to be. But the game fails to convey ANY of that to the player until Zephetto just... hints at it. That's it. And then we don't get anything else about it until we actually fight the first Starless Dark Falz, Vael, and that's still just a hint. Just a quick flashback to who we used to be. And it kinda sucks.

PSO2 NGS suffers from uninteresting writing with baseless connections to the past, rarely any good content, and a ton of reuse at a level that would make RGG Studios cringe. With its core combat, there is very little mechanical depth, and the game can be boiled down to mash attack 1 to win.

But that core combat does feel fluid. Attacks feel good to unleash. And above all that, the eye candy is absolutely remarkable, and the character creator is absolutely amazing. It's just the most beautiful, shallow puddle of a game that could be better. And knowing SEGA, this game CAN be better.

I don't recommend NGS at all, but I highly recommend getting into base PSO2 if you want to see what we had before the utter mess that NGS is.

Combat

In terms of Combat, NGS can be a bit boring and samey, but it still manages to be fun. The main problem is that not all weapons are viable. Talis, Launcher, Wand, Bow and TMG (Twin Mech Guns) all suffer from low DPS. The newest hotness is the recently released Slayer. 

Overall, combat is very simplistic with spamming photon arts and your weapon action. Outside of a few instances like hunter using their photon / weapon arts as a counter instead of the weapon action and techter having to occasionally charge their techniques to infuse their weapon, the only class I feel really plays differently is probably the bouncer's soaring blade. That's because the parry frames on it are a 1 time only use during a long photon art animation and much tighter than other frames. It also is one of the few classes that feels like it relies on a step dodge rather than a weapon parry action.

For the most part you're spamming photon arts and normal attacks and that's it. In the case of forces and techniques, you're matching elements. Enemy weak to ice? Use barta. Enemy weak to fire? Use foie. Outside of spamming zonde (an electric attack that chains to enemies) during PSE bursts (an event that happens in combat zones where hundreds of mobs spawn as you kill them in waves, ie think of D4 helltide events), you really have very little reason to use an element the enemy is not weak to. Combat is fun, but simplistic but also gets boring.

World:

The world of NGS is open world and split into 3 types of areas. Cities, Exploration zones and Combat zones. Combat zones are small areas where PSE bursts can happen and where the bulk of the rare weapons and stuff are farmed. PSE bursts provide a boss at the end with a chance to be upgraded to an "F" type burst which means that all enemies will be "Gold" variants. Enemies have "rare" forms that aren't actually all that rare which are just silver / gold reskins that have more HP and drop more meseta and experience and have a higher drop rate with an almost guaranteed weapon drop that gives you experience (gold primm / silver primm weapons) you use to level up your existing weapon.

The problem with the world design is that largely it's boring. The open worlds are static, never changing and the exploration zones suffer from very little incentive to do anything in them other than gather materials you use to refine your weapons, unlock potentials etc. Combat zones are where you get drops and exploration zones are where you mine minerals and stuff that respawn on a daily / weekly basis.

This could be improved if the zones had some identities to them, but sadly they don't. Exploration zones since Stia have slowly been updated having "giga recon" units and also where "malevolent" enemies spawn which are enemies that have much more defense, HP and hit like a truck  providing some challenge but the main issue is that the big bad malevolents only spawn on random thunderstorm events and aren't always up. 

Combat zones on the other hand are incredibly boring as they expect you to run around a small isolated zone for hours on end farming drops, meseta etc. Unlike PSO2 or PSO from dreamcast / gamecube,  there are no maps here with random patterns and variations. It's just a static zone that you run a circuit in where enemies spawn until you fill a gauge that goes up and down randomly and then complete a trial which boosts it to 5 and triggers a PSE burst. 

Urgent Quests:


One of the biggest issues with PSO2 NGS is that some of the most fun quests are "urgent quests." These are instanced based missions with up to 8 players to where you usually run through some mobs and fight a big boss at the end or just fight a big boss. Think of it like FFXIV's trials if you will. 8 people vs big boss. The difference is that instead of always being available, these uregent quests are hid behind a time gate and only available at certain times. You can get triggers to manually trigger the quest to be available, but the problem with that is they're limited from the alliance shop which you get medals from doing quests for your alliance (guild essentially.) Due to this, you only get so many a day so unless you save up you have to buy them off the shop. 

This also means that if you have a full time job or any type of downtime, you miss urgent quests. This can be a problem when some gear is locked behind urgent quests as the 8* weapon series Neos Astraean weapons were. These should really just be quests that are available all the time imo or triggers made more available.

Itemization and progression: 

The itemization and gearing progression in NGS is..Bad. Compared to original PSO where you  had weapons with unique abilities like the Tsumikiri J sword, Heaven's Punisher and Spread Needle, in NGS weapons have "potentials" that you can unlock. These are usually various types of potency boosts which increases your overall damage and give you an effect of some kind. This can range from healing 4% of your HP every 10 seconds to having a chance to not consume  healing items when using them to granting extra attacks every 5-15 seconds etc.

Ideally this would sound good except that one of the main problems is gear is quickly left behind with the update schedule NGS has. On top of that, SEGA is bad about giving out free equipment that is almost best in slot or the catch-up gear that's given out is usually as good or almost good as best in slot gear to the point to where it is almost beneficial to not play the game.

Instead of having a tanky build, everyone builds their weapons with augments (bonuses you put into weapon slots you get as you level the weapon) with the same stuff so there really is no "tank build" or "evasion build" etc. Essentially, everyone uses the same weapon, usually the latest released weapon and then augments it with the exact same capsules which are all attack power. The game suffers from far, far too many useless augment capsules that have no use. This isn't even getting into the grind that best in slot augments require which means they need hundreds if not thousands of other capsules to get the best chance of them going on your gear. There is a % system at play here to slot them in and that means if it isn't 100% it can fail which means you wasted hours of grinding or millions of meseta depending.


Cash Shop / F2P Friendly:


This game, in my opinion, isn't all that free to play friendly. It can be in the right circumstances but a lot of key features are hidden behind premium or passes you have to buy with AC, the cash shop currency Arks Cash. The biggest issue is the auction house / market being locked behind a paywall except for the 3 day shop pass you get from the mission pass every once in a while. 

On top of that, the game does occasionally have special scratches to where you can get overpowered augments that are better than everything in game. The only way to get them is through the cash shop in which whales will buy them and sell them on the market. A F2P can't get them otherwise and once that banner / scratch ticket is over, the augments are no longer available and the price skyrockets. 



FOMO. Fomo Everywhere:


One of the biggest issues NGS has is that it focuses on limited time content rather than static or long-lived content. They are always doing some sort of copy / paste seasonal event to where you have a point shop, you kill enemies or do the limited time quest to collect points and buy stuff from the shop, usually needing around 2-4 million points to buy it out. These events usually last 1-2 months and after a few weeks they refresh the shop with more of the same goods at higher prices so you have to farm more.

Conclusion:

With the combat feeling samey, the world being lackluster and not having any real defining features and SEGA constantly feeling like they're just throwing stuff at the wall to see what sticks, I honestly can't in good faith recommend the game at this time.

basic items that are available for in-game currency in japan, are only available for cash in this version. and not re-salable on the player market.

Phantasy Star Online 2 is a long running Sci-Fi Action MMORPG. It is a gorgeously looking game that allows for a one of a kind character customization and a simple yet compelling storyline to follow. The Gameplay is fun, interactive and many times chaotic, but you'll find friends who will make the game experience good for you. There's two game modes: The classical PSO2(known as base) and the recent addition of New Genesis that is a modern take of PSO2. Base offers ten years of content and a myriad of quests to keep the player entertained. NGS is relatively fresh and is still in active development. People will cite that NGS does not have as much content as the classic, but I feel this is an unfair take as the classic had nine years whereas NGS is entering their second year in development. Credit is given where credit is due, NGS have amazing potential and their QoLs are genuinely good.

There's quite a bit of a con in both PSO2Base and PSO2NGS. PSO2NGS is concurrently severely snail-pacingly slow in updates, and at most they'll have no issues shoving 3-4-5-6 AC tickets in your face in every headline. While I understand a business has to have a money model to function and I personally do support the model, there should be more than one Urgent update every five months. The previews are cool when they actually arrive, however, it is simply too slow to keep an active playerbase flowing in. The second con is that SEGA have now started to go back to old roots of adding a DPS meter to everything, and as a result, many of the elite groups are now damage parsing you using illegal third parties to check if you are doing enough damage or making sure that -you aren't holding them back-(though you're likely going to be the one reviving them time and time again.) I personally hate this kind of mechanic in games. We're not playing E-Sports, there's no reason to go super hard on a game with barely any development in it. The classes are vastly improved from base, now offering fun and quirky ways to hack 'n slash, though there's some concerns over Bouncer and Waker overpowering the rest of the classes. The state of the base version is incredibly inflated and only a handful of people now play it actively, resulting in many things being lost or being too hard for new people to do due to lack of people. Fortunately, there's been somewhat of a small rise of them. Inflation is still heavy.

[h1] A Fan's Preamble[/h1]

I wanna make it clear that I care immensely about this game. Or at least it's franchise, Phantasy Star has always been one of my favorite game series. Phantasy Star Online on the Dreamcast especially is a game that I loved playing as a child. At the time, I didn't even realize online co-op was something possible, let alone the games selling point. Despite this, the gameplay itself was so satisfying, with it's relative simplicity. Even today the combat still has some amazing staying power, and being able to play that game online now thanks to private servers feels like finding a hidden passage in your childhood home.

It was a wild ride between PSO2's localization to NGS, But finally, this game is at a point where I feel a review is warranted.

The most recent update as of this review was being tentatively called the "Ultra Evolution Update" before release. Which is a title more loaded than Jeff Bezo's wallet. Before the update, the lead developer came out and said that this is how they intended the game to be released on day one. Meaning that despite the game being branded "Ver. 2", it is effectively version 1.0.0.

So here we are. For all intents and purposes, the game has exited it's early access and is a "finished" product. So after most of the bugs, drama, and insane content droughts, is the game worth playing?

Well, you've already seen my answer. So let's talk about why:

[h1] Combat[/h1]

Firstly and most importantly, the combat is incredibly BORING. Despite having seemingly simpler combat, PSO achieved a fun system by making it heavily timing focused. Giving combat a nice rhythm. PSO2 made this timing more forgiving, but NGS has completely ditched this important aspect in exchange for focusing entirely on making attacks "look flashy". This flashy presentation, and increased combat abilities make the gameplay seem more in depth on the surface, but is in fact so shallow that the game gives you an "AUTO FIGHT" button that you can simply hold down to win. Even without this cruise control gameplay, trying to play the game skillfully amounts to very little more than cycling through which button you hold down.

It's doesn't help that most enemies are either worthless trash, or annoying damage sponges. The standard enemy  feels like it takes 30 seconds to whack away at until they keel over. In PSO, a foe like this would be a miniboss. Something that was an actual threat. Rather than the most basic enemy you find everywhere.

[h1] Progression[/h1]

Second most important aspect of a good MMO is a game's progression. AKA, how it feels to get stronger through the game, or, the enjoyability of grinding. Another way of thinking of it is how the game escalates. In this aspect the game still falls flat on it's face.

The dungeon crawling of previous games was a large part of previous games identity. With NGS, the removal of this shows how much heavy lifting that gameplay "format" was doing.

Grinding entails running around a small room, killing monsters, until the big monsters come out, repeating ad nauseum. The drops of these monsters are so minuscule and rare, that you might as well be collecting wads of gum in a McDonald's Drive-thru. Same also goes with their EXP payouts, which compounds this games massive issues with leveling.

Throughout the games 4-5 hour story, (which we will talk about next) you go from level 1 to level 60. With the current max being 70 (soon to be 75) Most of this leveling is skipped through massive EXP payouts skipping upwards of 10-20 levels at a time. However, it should be noted that levels in this game are mostly just an arbitrary number to lock you out of content. Paling in comparison to how important levels were in PSO2 let alone PSO where the massive dopamine rush of a level up was aided by [url=https://youtu.be/zQQ9bnksTPE] the best level-up jingle mankind ever created [/url]. It's almost as if the developers knew they made leveling a chore, and decided they could simulate the dopamine hit from previous game by force-feeding tons of levels at once.

[h1] Story[/h1]

NGS's story is at best a 4-5 hour affair. And any extra time spent is because of you being arbitrarily locked from progressing until you reach a certain power level. The actual plot consists of you -an amnesia ridden, silent protagonist- and two, one note, waifu-bait, party members (Aina and Manon), going from region to region solving problems that have no real bearing on an overarching plot or theme. Never do you face actual conflict because, as the protagonist, you are a perfect paragon of infinite power. Never flinching, even when facing revelations that should rock your world.  [spoiler] I.E. Being a test tube baby. [/spoiler] You never get a chance to role play the character you want to be. As you are almost always given dialogue choices that mean the exact same thing, to which characters respond in the exact same way regardless of choice. It's so insane how railroaded your character is in the story. So much so, that I would've preferred not having any dialogue options, so as to make the cutscenes shorter and, more bearable.

I could rant for hours on how terrible the story is, but I'm hitting the character limit so lets move on:

It's worth covering the new stuff in this game that was apparently worthy of calling it "Ver 2" so lets go over those:

 [h1] Cell-Shading [/h1]

This blatant attempt to make the game more superficially similar to Genshit Impact is an addition that completely destroys what little visual identity this game still had. You see, the filter gives all the games character that soft look which cell-shading excels at. However, it does nothing to the surrounding world. Making the characters clash with the environment to an extreme degree. It's about as jarring as it would be to see an actual anime character walking around in the real world.

Okay, with that, lets talk about the actual big new thing in this update:

 [h1] Creative Spaces[/h1]

Creative spaces were added to the game as a response to the massive player requests for personal quarters to make a comeback from PSO2. However, it seems the devs didn't understand why people wanted this feature, so creative spaces are a massive over correction to the perceived "hole" in the game.

Creative spaces throw out the apartment you were given to decorate in PSO2 and replaces it with a whole island. Far more space, and far more flexibility is given to you to create the home you want. And surprisingly, it doesn't require you a premium account to actually have fun with the feature.

Don't get me wrong, creative spaces are very fun to build in and to explore. So fun. in fact. that it overshadows the ACTUAL GAME attached. Even so, the creative spaces aren't anything that other games haven't done before. This is no better than freaking Disney Infinity's sandbox.

 [h1] Closing Thoughts (and TL;DR) [/h1]

 Hopping on the treadmill of completing dailies and spending real money for AC is a serious self abuse if it's in hopes for this game to ever become popular or have more to do in it. More meaningful and impactful story. classes are simplified, which sounds absolutely great considering PSO2 wasn't welcoming to players unfamiliar with its MH-like combat...

rare drops aren't special anymore, and the truly rare drops that would drive you insane are either 1) useless because they are outperformed by lower-rarity items or 2) outlandishly expensive and unaffordable for 99% of the population (and still useless).
